News.title: Labour slammed as hypocritical over massive political donations from trade unions
News.content:
Next

LABOUR has been slammed as hypocritical over massive political donations.

The Government has said £72million given to Reform by two crypto billionaires is a bid to buy influence.



But Labour has received nearly £43million from unions since 2020 — and introduced laws those organisations had campaigned for.

Labour’s Employment Rights Act 2025 makes it easier for unions to recruit, ballot for industrial action and call rolling strikes.



This week, senior minister Louise Haigh told unions that Labour will make it harder for firms to block requests to work from home.

The announcement was hailed by Trades Union Congress chief Paul Nowak.

But Reform’s Robert Jenrick said the Government’s “hypocrisy is off the charts”.

Shadow Business Secretary Julia Lopez said: “Unions are back pulling the strings, dictating policy.”

But Labour and the TUC said their funding is the “cleanest money” in politics.

Labour added: “There’s a world of difference between money donated by hundreds of thousands of nurses, cleaners and teaching assistants through unions, and millions of pounds donated to Reform by a handful of crypto billionaires.



“Labour will never shy away from standing up for working people.”

News.title: Girl, 2, dies after being pulled from neighbour’s swimming pool as devastated family mourn ‘unimaginable tragedy’
News.content:
POOL TRAGEDY Girl, 2, dies after being pulled from neighbour’s swimming pool as devastated family mourn ‘unimaginable tragedy’







Next

A TWO-YEAR-OLD girl has tragically died after being found in a pool in Texas.

The child was found in a pool by paramedics at Pine Trace Court, in the Atascocita South area of Harris County but it remains unclear how she ended up there.



Her grandmother was in the backyard with the children when she got distracted briefly, an investigator said to KHOU 11.

The family began looking for the little girl after the grandma had lost sight of her.



Just a few minutes later the family checked the garden next door because they knew there was an open swimming pool.

Unfortunately when they reached the pool, the girl was submerged in the water.

Her family repeatedly attempted CPR whilst waiting for emergency services to arrive.

The pool was reportedly in the backyard of a vacant home that was being remodelled.

Constable Mark Herman shared on social media that authorities responded to reports of a child found in a pool around 6pm on Friday afternoon.

Authorities closed the West Lake Houston Parkway, near FM 1960, to allow a Life Flight helicopter to land safely and rush the toddler to Memorial Hermann Hospital.



Locals were advised to avoid the area and expect delays.

Herman wrote on X for everyone to pray for the child and the family.

Despite doctors working tirelessly to administer life-saving treatment, the child sadly died several hours later.

Herman wrote on X: “It is with heavy hearts that we share the tragic update that the 2-year-old child has been pronounced deceased following an incident…where the child was found in a swimming pool.

“This is an unimaginable tragedy, and our hearts are with this child’s family during this incredibly difficult time.



“We ask our community to keep the family, loved ones and everyone affected by this heartbreaking loss in their thoughts and prayers.”

Harris County officials have not publicly identified the 2-year-old.

News.title: Foreign citizen being let-off by court mocks the British values that Sir Winston Churchill fought for
News.content:
Next

WHAT is going on in Britain when a foreign citizen can climb all over Winston Churchill’s statue, daub it with mad slogans and then get let off by the courts?

Olax Outis from the Netherlands covered the Westminster statue with phrases including “stop the genocide” and called Churchill a “Zionist war criminal” but was this week found not guilty of criminal damage.



War criminal? Wait till he finds out who Churchill defeated.

If it hadn’t been for Sir Winston, the virtue-signalling scumbag would be speaking German not Dutch.



And across the road from this statue, guess what our MPs have been talking about in Parliament?

You’d hope they’d be working flat out on the economy, the cost of living and finding jobs for the million young unemployed. Or maybe crime and immigration.



But no. As usual, it’s Israel and Palestine — a conflict over 2,000 miles away most of them know nothing about.

Birmingham MPs Tahir Ali and Ayoub Khan want ­Britain to take military action against Israel.

That renowned legal scholar Alastair Campbell and Sadiq Khan accused Israel of committing genocide.

The Mayor of London can’t stop kids shooting and stabbing each other in the capital but thinks people will listen when he calls for a ceasefire in the Middle East.



Wars are terrible. Tragically, innocent people get hurt. But Israel has not carried out a genocide.

In fact, a smaller proportion of civilians have been killed in Gaza than in any other recent conflict.

Even according to the Hamas health ministry, about three per cent of Gaza’s population has been killed in this war, many of them terrorists.



In the Holocaust, about 95 per cent of Poland’s Jews were killed. That was a genocide. Imagine trying to defeat the Nazis with this lot wringing their hands.

They’d demand a ceasefire and aid sent to the Germans.

There’d be a judicial review, Churchill would be in the dock and Hitler would be marching down Whitehall.

Israel is fighting for its life against terrorist armies equipped and trained by Iran. They want to wipe it off the map and murder every Jewish citizen.

Let’s be clear about this: Singling out the world’s only Jewish state and holding it to standards never applied to any other country is racism.



Even worse, falsely accusing it of the most appalling behaviour leads to anti- Jewish racism in Britain.

That’s why we end up with Jewish kids attacked on their way to school and synagogues fire-bombed. And it’s why a lunatic murdered ­people outside a synagogue in Manchester last year.

We might not be at war with Iran, but they have ­certainly declared war on us.

Israel is the front line, but extremists in Iran, Qatar and the Muslim Brotherhood hate the West and are fuelling extremism and pumping out propaganda to undermine it.

Keffiyeh-clad clowns on British campuses swallow their lies. Gullible young people are being radicalised.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

This nonsense is taking over the courts and politics, ordinary people are being ignored and, if we don’t all get a grip, our country will be changed forever.

We face a stark choice: Are we going to defend ­British values, our freedoms and the West’s way of life — just as Churchill did?

News.title: Christy Kinahan ordered to leave Dubai after visa revoked with gangster running scared amid €5m bounty & passport probe
News.content:
SAY YOUR DUBAIS Christy Kinahan ordered to leave Dubai after visa revoked with gangster running scared amid €5m bounty & passport probe







Next

GODFATHER Christy ‘The Dapper Don’ Kinahan has been ordered to leave Dubai.

Kinahan – the founder of Ireland’s deadliest narco terrorist gang – was ordered to leave the United Arab Emirates two weeks ago after having his residency revoked.



Although his residency in the UAE expired in April, he was able to appeal that decision in the Dubai courts.

But it’s believed he lost his final appeals in recent weeks.



After his visa had expired, he was also hit with a financial penalty for overstaying his visa.

It’s not clear if he paid any fines to the UAE.



One theory is that he could return to the UK.

Although he still has a €5m bounty on his head from the US authorities, he’s not the subject of any charges in the UK.

But he is still under investigation by the Spanish police into travelling on a false passport.

One source said: “Christy Kinahan’s time in Dubai has come to an end.



“The only reason he went there in the first place is because he wanted to keep out of reach of law enforcement in Europe.

“The authorities in Dubai want him out because he is seen as toxic despite his links to big business and senior industry and political figures in the country.

“He still has a bounty on his head and who knows where he could end up.”



Kinahan, 69, who was described in secret Spanish police files as the head of the ‘Irish Mafia’, has been living in the UAE for the last ten years.

Although he has previously flown to Holland during his time in the Middle East, he has rarely left his desert bolt-hole.

Kinahan had been flying on a British passport and had been connected to the region since 2007 – often making frequent flights before making his stay permanent in 2016.

On the rare occasions he did leave Dubai, it was to attend conferences on the airline industry in Zimbabwe when he posed as a legitimate businessman.

The decision to deport him from the country he called home has now left his youngest son, Christopher, 45, isolated.



The source added: “Christopher Junior will be coming under even more pressure now.”

The last two times the Dapper Don was in Ireland was in October 1997 when he attended his father’s funeral and also for his youngest son’s wedding in 2006.

He moved to the Costa del Sol permanently over 25 years ago where he laid the foundations for his criminal organisation’s billion euro empire.

He made the decision to move to Spain over fears he and other senior members of the gang could be arrested in Ireland.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But they later left Spain after Gardai increased their international outreach by forging close relationships with their counterparts in the UK, Holland and Spain.



Although one of the world’s most wanted men, Christy Kinahan also spent his time in Dubai leaving online restaurant reviews.

News.title: Families with eight kids or more raking in extra £21,800 a YEAR after two child benefit cap axed
News.content:
Next

THOUSANDS of families with eight or more children get an extra £21,800 a year after Labour axed the two-child benefit cap.

Ex-PM Sir Keir Starmer caved in to backbenchers when his Government was on the rocks and cut the policy, at a cost of some £3billion per year.



Universal Credit figures show 2,200 families with eight children or more now receive £21,883 extra annually.

This amounts to around £29,178 in total — the starting salary of a police constable in Essex or Kent after tax.



They are among the 17,290 families with six children or more receiving at least an extra £14,589 per year.

When that is added to their benefits they get for their first two kids, it comes to £21,883.

The two-child cap was introduced by the Tories and stopped parents claiming payments worth about £300 a month for more than two kids.

Helen Whately, Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary, said: “Hard-working parents don’t get a pay rise from their employer when they have another child, but Labour has done just that for people on benefits.”

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has vowed to reinstate the cap to fund defence.

In today’s Sun on Sunday, she writes: “We believe those on benefits should have to make the same choices about having children as those who aren’t.”



A government source said large families are less than one per cent of all Universal Credit households with children.

The Department for Work and Pensions said: “Almost 60 per cent of households benefitting from the two-child limit removal have at least one parent in work.

“This change gives hard-working families extra breathing room, lifting 450,000 children out of poverty.”

News.title: Earl Spencer accuses King of ‘gaslighting’ him after Charles suggests explosive book is ‘clouded by grief’
News.content:
Next

EARL Spencer has accused King Charles of “gaslighting” him in a fresh blow to the royals as the row over Diana’s memoir continues.

The Earl made the accusation in response to the Palace’s statement over the claims made in his memoir titled Swan Song: Diana, My Sister.



The author – who said the then-Prince told him “we’ll forget her soon enough” after her death – stood by his claims this evening.

He also claimed Diana, who died in a car crash in Paris in 1997, would be “cheering from the rafters” at his book.



It comes after Buckingham Palace issued a furious riposte to the allegation, made in a book the 62-year-old author, Diana’s brother, will publish next week.

A spokesman for the King, in an unusual move, said Charles was “mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason.”



Speaking to The Mail, the Earl said: “It is not every day you wake up to find you’ve been gaslit by the King.

“It was astonishingly provocative and below the belt because it was essentially trying to say I’d lied without the King being able to deny what I’d said.”



Earl Spencer also claimed money, including a reported advance of up to £1million, had “never even been the remotest consideration.”

He added: “My motivation in this book has been to tell the truth about Diana and all she had to put up with in her public life through the eyes of the brother who grew up with her.”

And, claiming Diana would have supported the book, called Swan Song, he added: “People are missing a fundamental point, which is that Diana was my sister and I have every right to write about my own sister.

“I can tell you that Diana would be cheering from the rafters at this book.

“I have no doubt about that.”



This comes as King Charles told Earl Spencer he was “lucky” to have inherited his fortune so young, the author has claimed.

Princess Diana’s brother, 62, said the alleged comments left him “surprised” after his father, the eighth Earl Spencer, died aged 68 in 1992.

Spencer, who was 27 at the time, told US TV network CBS: “It was a very peculiar conversation, actually, because my father had died very suddenly a few days before.

“And I just was so surprised, because Prince Charles, as he was then, said to me, ‘You’re so lucky.’

And I said, ‘I’m so sorry, sir.’ And he said, ‘You are so lucky to have inherited so young’.”



Earl Spencer is set to bash the King further in a BBC interview broadcast tomorrow evening.

But a friend of the King, who last week hosted an AI summit in Scotland, hit back, telling The Sunday Times: “He is saddened that the sorrows of old are being dragged up again.

“The King was rather more concerned about the future of mankind than the unkind claims of one man picking at the scars of the past.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Buckingham Palace, in a rare move to answer allegations, denied claims made against the King last week.

It said: “His Majesty is mindful the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss.”

News.title: Threat from Russia is growing and there is no urgency from the PM… he has shown a total failure to lead on defence
News.content:
Next

ANDY BURNHAM didn’t misspeak when he told me that “our national ­security cannot come at the expense of our social security”.

He was finally being honest with the country about where his priorities lie.



I couldn’t believe the words that had come out of his mouth.

Labour MPs, on the other hand, cheered . . . apparently forgetting that those words weren’t just heard in Westminster or Manchester; they were also heard in Moscow.



If it’s a choice between funding defence and funding more benefits, Burnham is picking benefits every time.

And Vladimir Putin is watching, just as he is watching what’s happening across Europe.



On Friday, French President Emmanuel Macron said France had been targeted by Russian attacks in the past few weeks, and he ordered a plan to protect French critical infrastructure and defence industry sites.

Days earlier the Polish Prime Minister, Donald Tusk, had told his MPs that Russia was planning drone and missile strikes on countries supporting Ukraine.

On September 1, Germany said they suspected Russia was responsible for a drone attack at Leipzig airport in August.

The threat is very real and it’s growing. Yet we see no urgency at all from the Labour Government.



In fact, we see the opposite.

There remains a £5billion hole in the already inadequately funded “Defence Investment Plan”, and whenever I ask Andy Burnham about the need to increase defence spending, he tells me he’s committed to meeting the Nato target in 2035.

2035? That’s almost a decade away!

It was Keir Starmer who told the country that our intelligence services believed there could be an attack by Russia on Nato as soon as 2030, meaning Britain would be at war.

Now, while France and Poland increase the pace of their war readiness, at the start of this month the British Army had to stop non-essential training exercises to save money.



Burnham’s response? “Ask me again in ten years.”

I don’t say this lightly, but the PM is putting our national security and the safety of everyone in Britain at risk by making defence spending a lower priority than welfare.

Worse still, he thinks he can get away with it. Labour MPs are right behind him on this issue.



Remember, it was the Welfare Secretary Pat McFadden who said that, at every meeting with Labour MPs, they would ask him: “Who can we tax in order to pay benefits to others?”

This is a total failure of leadership from Burnham.

Defence of the nation is the first duty of government.

We need to increase our defence spending every year so we get to three per cent of GDP by 2030. Anything after that is too late.

John Healey resigned as Defence Secretary at the start of summer because he agreed with that statement.



In fact, he said the Government’s plans would make our country and our troops “less safe”.

That must have been a different John Healey from the one now in 11 Downing Street who is suddenly fine with a plan the other John Healey resigned over.

Finding the money to pay for defence means making tough choices . . . something Burnham is reluctant to do.



Two weeks ago, I set out how the Conservatives will get defence spending to three per cent of GDP by 2030 and how we would pay for it.

We are not afraid of difficult decisions. It’s what we are elected to do. It means cutting the bloated welfare budget so we can give our troops the equipment, housing and training they need.

I had already announced that the Conservatives would reinstate the two-child benefit cap, because we believe that those on benefits should have to make the same choices about having children as those who aren’t.

Added to that we have a plan to change housing benefit so that those on benefits have to make the same decisions on where they can afford to live as those who aren’t.

Alongside junking the disastrous £35billion Chagos deal and repurposing the money ploughed into Net Zero projects for a sovereign defence fund,



I have shown that hitting three per cent by the end of the decade can be done and how we should do it. If I can do this, why can’t Andy Burnham?

And let’s not forget, three per cent is just the minimum our country needs to stay safe.

The Government must now explain what it knows about the escalations in Eastern Europe, how it assesses the threat posed by Russia, and what it plans to do about it.

In the meantime, the Conservatives are gearing up.

My new Shadow Foreign Secretary Tom Tugendhat, and Shadow Defence Secretary James Cartlidge, are working with purpose on more plans to keep our country safe.



We know that after Labour makes a mess, Conservatives have to clean it up.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

So we are ready, we will put national security first, and even work with the Government where necessary to ensure our country is properly defended.

It remains to be seen if Burnham will take up that offer.

News.title: Andy Burnham to channel Barack Obama with speech ‘all about hope’ at Labour conference
News.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham plans to channel former US President Barack Obama and make his debut Labour conference speech “all about hope”.

The new Labour PM is facing a big test as he sets out his stall to the party faithful at their annual get-together in Liverpool next week.



Government insiders said he plans to “do a Barack Obama” and promise to “inject hope” back into the country in his hotly-anticipated address.

Barack Obama’s 2008 US Presidential campaign centred around the message of “hope and change”.



It was famously captured in the iconic red and blue poster of Obama’s portrait with the word hope emblazoned underneath.

A senior Labour Party source said: “Andy’s plan to try to do a Barack Obama and make his speech theme all about hope.

“They want to draw a line under the gloom of Keir Starmer’s time in No10. They want to make it all about hope – the vibes of Obama’s 2008 campaign.”

It also echoes Bill Clinton’s 1992 campaign for the White House, in which the hopeful famously declared “I still believe in a Place Called Hope”.

Bill Clinton grew up in a town called Hope in Arkansas.

Mr Burnham ousted Sir Keir and became PM in July, and since then he has tried to strike a very different tone to the Starmer regime.

He says he wants to put “hope in every heart” and spent his first month in No10 announcing small, popular measures to ease the cost of living crisis, such as a £2 cap on bus fares.



But critics have attacked his premiership – saying ‘vibes’ and slick TikTok videos are no substitute for carrying out the public and economic reforms needed.

News.title: Northern Quarter: Air ambulance lands on top of Manchester car park and street is shut off
News.content:
An air ambulance seen on the top floor of the Northern Quarter multi-storey car park

Emergency services attended an incident at the Northern Quarter car park in Manchester city centre, with an air ambulance seen landing on the top deck

Northern Quarter: Air ambulance lands on top of Manchester car park and street is shut off

A large emergency services presence was reported at a multi-storey car park in Manchester city centre.

An air ambulance was seen landing on the top deck of the Northern Quarter car park on Saturday evening. Cordons were put in place on Church Street, near the car park entrance, and on Turner Street, outside the Abel Heywood pub.

Pictures from the scene showed several police cars and ambulances in attendance, the Manchester Evening News reports. Officers remained at the scene at around 9pm on Saturday.

The Mirror has contacted Greater Manchester Police for further information.

News.title: Manchester Airport live: Delays to flights after repair work to runway
News.content:
One of Manchester Airport's runways was closed to 'allow routine maintenance to take place'

There have been widespread delays at Manchester Airport tonight, with both arrivals and departures affected following repair work on one of the airport's runways

Manchester Airport is experiencing widespread flight disruption tonight following repair work on one of its runways.

An airport spokesperson told the Mirror that one of the runways was closed for a short period today to "allow routine maintenance to take place", describing the work as a "quick repair to a minor issue".

According to the airport's website, both departures and arrivals are facing major delays, with several outbound flights held up by more than an hour.

News.title: Missing schoolgirl Lillia, 13, found after eight-day search as police issue statement
News.content:
Missing schoolgirl Lillia, 13, found after eight-day search as police issue statement

Lillia Lloyd Walton, 13, who had been missing for more than a week has been found 'safe and well' in Manchester city centre, police said

View 2 Images Lillia Lloyd Walton, 13, has been found (Image: Greater Manchester Police)

A 13-year-old girl who had been missing for more than a week has been found "safe and well" in Manchester city centre, police said.

‌



Lillia Lloyd Walton was reported missing by her family last Friday (September 11) after leaving her family home in Bolton, Greater Manchester.

‌



In a statement on Saturday night, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said: "Thank you to everyone who shared our missing appeal for 13-year-old Lillia, who has been missing since Friday 11 September 2026.

‌



"We can confirm that she has been found safe and well in the city centre. She is currently with our officers, and her next-of-kin have been informed of this update. We will release more information in due course."

View 2 Images Lillia was seen on CCTV at Manchester Piccadilly bus station on Monday morning (Image: Greater Manchester Police)

‌



GMP revealed earlier on Saturday that Lillia had been seen on CCTV at Manchester Piccadilly bus station at 10.36am on Monday, September 14.

That sighting followed another one earlier that morning, when Lillia was seen boarding the number 36 bus from Salford.

Police distributed hundreds of missing person leaflets, issued social media appeals and worked with media outlets, and officers from the force's dedicated CCTV unit trawled through hours of footage.

Article continues below

Chief Superintendent Helen Critchley, of GMP’s Bolton district, thanked the public and the media for their support on Saturday.

She also thanked Lillia's mum, Jessica, for supporting police appeals over the past few days.

"She has shown incredible strength throughout, and we are doing all we can to bring her daughter back home to her," Ch Supt Critchley said.

News.title: Madeleine McCann prime suspect Christian Brueckner plots tell-all book in fresh agony for her parents
News.content:
Madeleine McCann prime suspect Christian Brueckner plots tell-all book in fresh agony for her parents

EXCLUSIVE: Christian Brueckner, who was released from jail a year ago this week, and the prime suspect for the disappearance of Madeleine McCann, wants a book to be published in both German and English

View 5 Images The sickening plan has sparked fury (Image: PA/PA Wire)

The prime suspect in the disappearance of Madeleine McCann is planning to publish a tell-all book - sparking fury.

‌



Christian Brueckner, who has never been charged over the youngster's disappearance, is penning his story just a year after he was released from prison for rape. Strict rules mean criminals cannot profit from their crimes, but rules in his native Germany are different, and it is feared Brueckner, 49, could earn a significant amount from the sickening release.

‌



Retired British police detective Kevin Moore told us: “I wont be buying it. It’s abhorrent.” Spooked locals in Brueckner’s homeland added: “It’s a disgrace.”

‌



Madeleine McCann suspect Christian Brueckner to be sent back to court for rape retrial READ MORE :

View 5 Images The sickening plan has sparked fury (Image: Phil Harris)

Insiders say the creep has already started putting pen to paper, and has approached at least one professional writer to help him craft the text. The deluded fiend has told pals he believes he could make a seven-figure sum - but in reality it would be a far more modest sum.

A source told the Mirror: “Brueckner is desperate to tell his side of the story. He believes that writing about his innocence will help him. He wants the book to be published in both German and English. Ultimately he also sees it as a way to help him financially as he has been unable to find any work since getting out of jail and is living on benefits.”

‌



Brueckner’s plan will cause further anguish for Madeleine’s parents, Kate and Gerry McCann, who still have no answers since their daughter went missing in May 2007. Retired Detective Chief Superintendent Mr Moore worked on hundreds of investigations, including the Babes in the Wood murders, which involved the sexual assault and strangulation of two nine-year-old schoolgirls.

Mr Moore said: “He is obviously a particularly unpleasant individual who was convicted of horrible crimes in the past. I assume he will obviously be writing about his innocence in the Madeleine McCann case. To me, it’s abhorrent. I won’t be buying it and one would hope the public won’t want to buy it.”

German prosecutors first named Brueckner as the prime suspect in the case in June 2020, but they were unable to stop him being released from prison after serving a seven-year sentence for the rape of an elderly pensioner in Praia da Luz, the same resort where Madeleine disappeared, in 2005.

‌



And despite claiming they believe he abducted and killed the then three-year-old, prosecutors have still not charged the convicted paedo and rapist with any offence in relation to the Madeleine investigation.

View 5 Images Madeleine's parents Kate and Gerry McCann (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

Brueckner was released from prison on September 17 last year. He has been unable to find work and has moved home several times after repeatedly being hounded out by locals who did not want him living near them. Protest group Victim Protection Before Perpetrator Protection are among those who have been campaigning to have Brueckner moved.

‌



Told about the fiend’s book plan, its co-leader Annika, who asked for her surname not to be published, said: “It’s a disgrace. This man is a convicted criminal, already convicted of many terrible offences, and yet now he gets to write a book and spout all his lies. It’s a slap in the face for the parents of Maddie and for everyone really.

“I think it’s unfair on the victims – they’ll suffer for the rest of their lives because of his actions, they’re being punished for it, and on top of that he’s writing a book about it. It’s now been a year and he’s just allowed to be out and roam free and do what he wants. One could really despair at it all.”

View 5 Images Brueckner pictured cycling near his home in northern Germany where he is living in fenced-off container accommodation

‌



Brueckner is now living in fenced-off container accommodation in northern Germany, where he is under 24-hour surveillance. He must wear an ankle tag for four more years and faces recall to prison if he breaks any of the conditions of his release, including moving house without telling probation staff.

Convicted criminals can legally write and publish books in Germany where freedom of expression and artistic freedom are protected by Germany’s constitution. But there are strict legal and financial limits — particularly when offenders attempt to turn their crimes into profit.

A book must still comply with German law and no glorification of crime is allowed. Criminal acts also cannot be presented in ways that themselves breach criminal law, including certain forms of glorification or material amounting to instructions for committing offences.

‌



View 5 Images Protest group Victim Protection Before Perpetrator Protection are among those who have been campaigning to have Brueckner moved from their area

Offenders cannot simply expose, insult or unlawfully violate the privacy and personality rights of their victims or victims’ families. Real names may therefore have to be changed or individuals anonymised, depending on the circumstances.

Where legally enforceable, victims can seek to seize the offender’s income — potentially including book royalties — to satisfy debts. Under certain circumstances, the state can also confiscate criminal proceeds and confiscate assets derived from criminal activity. Whether book income itself can be seized depends crucially on the legal connection between the money and the underlying offence.

Article continues below

In May, it was reported the Metropolitan Police was pushing for the German to be extradited to the UK to stand trial at the Old Bailey. A top Scotland Yard officer is said to be leading efforts to charge him on suspicion of abduction and murder ahead of the 20th anniversary of Madeleine’s disappearance next year.

But there is a major obstacle following Brexit, as the German constitution prevents the extradition of its citizens to non-EU countries. The Met is also said to be determined he will one day face charges in Germany.

Brueckner has always publicly denied any involvement in Madeleine’s disappearance and his lawyers have claimed he has been made a “scapegoat” by the authorities. He was living in a ramshackle farmhouse on the edge of Praia da Luz when the toddler vanished from the Ocean Club resort while her parents dined at a nearby tapas restaurant.

News.title: Folkestone hotel fire: Sleeping guests evacuated as fire rips through hotel in overnight chaos
News.content:
An overnight fire at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone has led to hundreds of guests being evacuated and the local council opening a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park

Fire crews battling a blaze at a Kent seafront hotel this morning have issued an "avoid the area" warning to the public.

Hundreds of guests staying at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone have been evacuated from the site following the overnight blaze, according to Folkestone and Hythe District Council.

The fire is believed to have started at around 1am on Saturday, with locals taking to social media to share images of the incident from afar. The cause of the fire has not yet been established.

Kent Fire and Rescue Service said 26 fire engines were used at the height of the blaze while crews wearing breathing apparatus worked to extinguish the fire.

A spokesperson for Folkestone and Hythe District Council said: "A fire is currently ongoing at the Folkestone Grand Burstin Hotel. We are operating a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park for people being evacuated from the site, where we are providing support to those affected.

"We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety."

News.title: Folkestone hotel fire being treated as suspicious, say police
News.content:
Folkestone hotel fire being treated as suspicious, say police

Police said a fire at a major seaside hotel, which forced around 280 people to evacuate, was being treated as suspicious

View 5 Images Police tape at the Grand Burstin Hotel on the Folkestone seafront (Image: Cover Images)

A blaze that ripped through a hotel on the Kent seafront is being treated as suspicious, police said.

‌



Around 280 people were evacuated from the Grand Burstin Hotel in The Harbour, Folkestone, just after 1am on Saturday where a fire is believed to have started in the basement, Kent Fire and Rescue Service said. Emergency services rushed to the scene and a welfare centre was set up by Folkestone and Hythe District Council.

‌



Kent Police, on Saturday afternoon, shared that a probe into the circumstances was launched while adding that officers believe the fire may have been caused deliberately. No injuries relating to the fire have been reported.

‌



At least 16 dead as huge fire rips through nursing home with residents trapped READ MORE :

View 5 Images Fire damage on the walls of the hotel (Image: Cover Images)

Kent Fire and Rescue Service said 26 fire engines were used at the height of the fire while crews wearing breathing apparatus were working to extinguish the blaze.

The hotel overlooks Folkestone's harbour and has 550 rooms, according to the Britannia Hotels website. Officers are in attendance to assist with traffic flow while crews from Kent Fire and Rescue Service work to fully extinguish the fire.

‌



View 5 Images Emergency services rushed to the scene at around 1am (Image: Cover Images)

Folkestone and Hythe District Council posted on X and said: "A fire is currently ongoing at the Folkestone Grand Burstin Hotel. We are operating a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park for people being evacuated from the site, where we are providing support to those affected.

"We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety.

‌



View 5 Images Around 280 people were evacuated from the hotel (Image: Cover Images)

"Our advice to residents living nearby is to: close all windows and doors; avoid the area and do not attempt to approach the hotel; follow the instructions of emergency services; keep roads clear to allow emergency vehicles to access the area. We will provide further updates as information becomes available."

In an update at 5:30pm, Kent Fire & Rescue said: "An investigation is underway to establish the cause of the fire at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone, which is being treated as suspicious."

‌



It added that four fire engines, a height vehicle and the technical rescue unit were at the scene, while firefighting operations were ongoing.

View 5 Images A welfare centre was set up by Folkestone and Hythe District Council (Image: Cover Images)

A spokesperson for Britannia Hotels Group said: "We can confirm there has been an incident at the Grand Burstin Hotel in Folkestone and we are taking immediate action to ensure the safety and wellbeing of all guests and team members.

Article continues below

"Emergency services are on site and we are fully co-operating with the authorities to support those affected and assist with the ongoing response."

Anyone who may have witnessed the incident or might have relevant CCTV or dashcam footage from the area, particularly from 10pm on Friday to 12.30am on Saturday, is urged to call Kent Police on 01843 222289 quoting 46/155727/26.

News.title: Jarrod Bowen's alternative marriage offer and saucy chant about Dani Dyer
News.content:
Jarrod Bowen's alternative marriage offer and saucy chant about Dani Dyer

West Ham legend Jarrod Bowen had an unusual marriage request shortly before tying the knot with Strictly Come Dancing star Dani Dyer

View 4 Images Jarrod Bowen and Dani Dyer have been an item since 2021 (Image: Jed Cullen/Dave Benett/Getty Images)

West Ham hero Jarrod Bowen actually had a wildly different proposal before marrying Dani Dyer in 2025. Reality TV star Dyer, 30, is back on screens on Saturday for Strictly Come Dancing.

‌



The daughter of acting icon Danny Dyer shot to fame after winning Love Island in 2018. Fast forward three years, and she met Hammers striker Bowen, 29, in 2021.

‌



Danny was clearly ecstatic at his daughter's choice of partner, being a West Ham fanatic. When the duo announced their engagement in 2024, after having twin daughters Star and Summer a year earlier, The Football Factory star jokingly claimed that Bowen should be marrying him instead.

‌



Ahead of the pair's nuptials, he told Closer: "I think I'm in love with him. He plays for West Ham and he's unbelievable, this guy. He comes in my house, I take his shoes off for him and I give him the remote control, and I say, ‘Mate, this is your house now.’ He's an incredible person.

"I can't wait to give Dani away, but I still think that he's marrying the wrong Danny Dyer. Honestly, I feel sorry for my other daughter, who's nearly 18, because she could never bring home a man to match what Jarrod’s done for me.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Jarrod Bowen could land Premier League return in £50m transfer despite contract vow READ MORE :

"She could bring home a heart surgeon or somebody who cures cancer and I’ll go, ‘Well, really? Jarrod's got the winning goal in a European final.’ I couldn't have written a better script. He's just such a beautiful man."

Danny's love for Bowen is shared by the Irons' faithful. Sections of the crowd often serenade the forward to the explicit chant: "Bowen's on fire, and he's s******g Dani Dyer" - to the tune of dance hit Freed from Desire.

View 4 Images Bowen has grown close to his West Ham-supporting father-in-law (Image: danidyerxx)

‌



Danny himself slightly restructured the song to make it more family-friendly during his father-of-the-bride speech at his daughter's wedding. On videos shared on social media, he could be heard urging guests to sing "Bowen's On Fire – and he's married Dani Dyer.'

After Bowen scored the late winner in West Ham's heroic 2-1 Europa Conference League final victory against Fiorentina in 2023, supporters once again sang the song. This time, Bowen was filmed jumping up and down to the chant.

Despite West Ham's relegation from the Premier League last season, Bowen signed a new deal with the East London club. He's started the Championship season in fine form, too.

‌



4 View 4 Images Danny Dyer led the chant at his daughter's wedding (Image: Instagram/) 4 View 4 Images Dani Dyer and Jarrod Bowen tied the knot in a stunning ceremony (Image: Danu Dyer Instagram / evieradfordsocials)

Yet Saturday night will see Dani take the stage after her stint on the BBC ballroom show was cut short last year due to injury. Such was its severity that she was ruled out of the show before the live shows even began.

Article continues below

Dani is now being given a second shot at being part of the BBC One dance show. She said: "If I'm really honest, my biggest fear is getting injured again. I'm going to do everything I can to look after myself, stay positive and just enjoy every moment of the experience."
