Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star lays into £75m man who was 'a million miles off it' at Brighton
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star lays into £75m man who was 'a million miles off it' at Brighton

Arsenal were well beaten by Brighton & Hove Albion as their 100% win record came to an end

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has been told one Arsenal star was 'miles off it' in the defeat to Brighton. (Image: (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP via Getty Images) )

Former Arsenal star Paul Merson has slammed Bruno Guimaraes for his display against Brighton and Hove Albion, insisting the Brazil international appeared 'a million miles off it. ' The Gunners were thrashed 3-0 by Fabian Hurzeler's side, suffering their first defeat of the season.

The Gunners had the opportunity to match a 123-year club record of eight consecutive victories across all competitions to begin a campaign, but Brighton dominated proceedings. Pascal Gross gave the hosts the lead after 31 minutes before Charalampos Kostoulas doubled their advantage on the stroke of half-time.

The Arsenal boss raced down the tunnel in a bid to rally his troops at the interval, but the Gunners were handed a dose of their own medicine when Chema Andres powered home a header from a corner shortly before the hour mark.

BBC forced to apologise live on air during Arsenal humiliation at Brighton READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta points finger at Arsenal stars as Gunners thumped by Brighton READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It proved a frustrating afternoon for Guimaraes on his maiden start for the club, losing possession just seven minutes into proceedings.

Kostoulas tried an ambitious effort from distance, but David Raya managed to push the shot over the crossbar, though it served as an ominous warning of what lay ahead.

Speaking on Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday about Guimaraes' performance, Merson said: "He was a million miles off it, million miles off it. I said at half-time that he'd come off but he stayed on another 10 minutes or so.

"No, it was really quick for him. They closed him down. I don't care how good you are, if people get your head down and close you down and make you work, it becomes a leveller.

"That's what Brighton have done. They haven't given anybody time on the ball to get their head up and pass it, and they've been absolutely brilliant."

View 2 Images Arsenal were thumped on a miserable afternoon at Brighton (Image: Getty Images)

Following the final whistle, a clearly frustrated Arteta pulled no punches, saying: "Extremely disappointed. But first of all, we have to congratulate Brighton; they deserved it.

"They were the better team, and from our side, there were certain basics in football that we didn't. Winning the first ball.

"They put us in a really difficult place. The amount of technical errors. We didn't respect any principle of play. We had moments of dominance and control, and we opened them up; we didn't take those chances."

When asked if it was the best result of his career, Seagulls' Fabian Hurzelersaid: "It is a difficult question to ask immediately after the game when the emotions are still high.

"It is very important to stay humble. We have to enjoy this moment but understand why we had success and come back to our roots, which is about being brilliant in the basics and trusting each other."

Sports.title: Curtain falls on historic Peters era at Hull KR
Sports.content:
In 2025 Hull KR became just the fifth team to win the Super League Grand Final in the 30 years of the competition.

That was thanks to the guidance of Willie Peters. In his third year in charge of the club, he helped them 'climb Everest' and make history.

Not only did they win the Betfred Super League, they picked up the League Leaders' Shield and Challenge Cup, and then topped that off with a World Club Challenge win over Brisbane Broncos.

Every trophy was theirs. They simply were the team to beat, but no one could.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League eliminator between Warrington Wolves and Hull KR as Matty Ashton's hat-trick helped the hosts book a semi-final against Leeds Rhinos

It was announced part way through this season that 2026 would mark Peters' final season in charge of the Robins before he heads to pastures new to take charge of the NRL's newest franchise, the PNG Chiefs.

The task was set: Finish on a high for their leader. Unfortunately for those from east Hull, they did not get the fairytale ending to close out Peters' four years in charge as they went out in the eliminators to Warrington Wolves after finishing sixth in the table.

However, Peters views it as "the best four years of his life" of which he is immensely proud.

"Discipline has cost us a lot this year, and unfortunately tonight, but I can't fault them," Peters told Sky Sports after the defeat at Warrington.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Peta Hiku is shown a straight red card for throwing a rabbit punch, leaving Hull KR down to 12-men in their Super League eliminator against Warrington Wolves

"I am really proud of them. They kept fighting to the end. Warrington played really well and have been a very good team all year. I wish them all the best, but I'm really, really proud of the group and proud of what they've achieved over the last four years at the club. We've made a lot of beautiful memories.

"When you're down to 12 men it makes it difficult, but we put ourselves in the game. We scored down the other end, went two points ahead and then, against the run of play, they scored.

"Fatigue always creeps in and it did towards the back end of the game. Peta (Hiku) has been great for us for three years. What he did [get sent off] was probably the wrong thing, but he's been outstanding for me over the last three years.

"We've got a lot of great memories, that's for sure, but they're still here, still cheering for their team. We're a close-knit club. We're a club that wanted to win trophies, and we have, but the fight tonight shows what this place is about.

"We were well beaten, but we still showed a lot of fight. My family and I have had an absolute ball. We've loved it over here and we'll never forget our time at Hull KR.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Burgess finishes a superb length-of-the-field Hull KR move after Arthur Mourgue slices through the Warrington defence

"I do feel loved, absolutely. Love's important. I remember Russell Crowe saying years ago at South (Sydney Rabbitohs) that it's all about the love, and there's something in that.

"When you're part of a family and create the right environment, especially in sport, where everyone cares about each other, you can do wonderful things.

"There's no doubt I've felt the love from the fans and the players, and vice versa. I love them too. When there's genuine care and love for each other, you can achieve special things.

"I love it over here. I'm really looking forward to the next chapter and to having a positive impact on a country (Papua New Guinea) through rugby league, both on and off the field.

"It's similar to what we've done here, but on a bigger scale. I'm really excited about that challenge."

Peters to return to Super League one day? 'Never say never'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League Grand Final between Hull KR and Wigan Warriors

While this particular chapter is closed for Peters and he has ticked off his goal of coaching in Super League, he admits he will never close the book on the UK.

But for now, he is focused on achieving the next goal which is being a head coach in the NRL.

Despite that, he will continue to back the European competition and ensure it gets the "recognition it deserves".

"We have loved it here. This has been home, and probably this year was the first time it really felt like home, which made it even harder knowing I was leaving. My family and I have loved it, so you never say never," he added.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Hull KR celebrate their historic domestic treble with a bus parade around the city

"I am proud. I've got a great support network and I've loved working with everyone. You've all been great. The rugby league community over here has been fantastic. The game is in a positive place and I think there's a lot of growth ahead in the next few years.

"The product is outstanding and it's finally getting the recognition it deserves, even in Australia.

"I don't think Super League has always received the respect it merits, but I've always respected it. That's why I played here and why I always wanted to coach here.

"I'm proud to have been involved in Super League as a coach, and now I've got some goals to tick off when I return to the NRL.

"Just thank you for the memories and thank you for the support they've given me. They've made me a better person and a better coach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the World Club Challenge between Hull KR and Brisbane Broncos

"I've now got an opportunity to return to the NRL, something I've always wanted to do, and it's purely because of what they've achieved.

"At the end of the day, the players decide how hard they want to work and where they want to get to, and they've been massive for me and my family.

"I also want to acknowledge the board, who have been incredibly supportive. Everyone at Hull KR, I'm going to miss dearly. Thank you to everyone, including the away fans. The support I've received has been incredible. So, thank you."

Sports.title: Warrington beat Hull KR to set up semi against Leeds as Hiku sees red
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League eliminator between Warrington Wolves and Hull KR as Matty Ashton's hat-trick helped the hosts book a semi-final against Leeds Rhinos Highlights of the Super League eliminator between Warrington Wolves and Hull KR as Matty Ashton's hat-trick helped the hosts book a semi-final against Leeds Rhinos

Warrington Wolves set up a Super League semi-final with Leeds Rhinos after a 35-12 victory over reigning champions Hull KR in their eliminator showdown at the Halliwell Jones Stadium.

It marks Warrington's first semi-final since 2024 after they missed out on the play-offs in 2025.

It also means Willie Peters' tenure as Robins head coach is now over after his reign which featured the history-making season in 2025 in which he won the Super League for the club for the first time.

The flashpoint of the game came early in the second half when Peta Hiku saw red for a punch on George Williams and the player advantage for Warrington eventually became too much for Hull KR to contend with.

Warrington had a narrow 12-6 lead at half-time thanks to a converted Ben Currie try, Ewan Irwin penalty and Matty Ashton's score. Hull KR hit back through a Joe Burgess wonder-try that was started by Arthur Mourgue to get themselves in the game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Peta Hiku is shown a straight red card for throwing a punch, leaving Hull KR down to 12 in their Super League eliminator against Warrington Wolves Peta Hiku is shown a straight red card for throwing a punch, leaving Hull KR down to 12 in their Super League eliminator against Warrington Wolves

After Hiku's red card, Ashton scored twice more to complete his hat-trick with Albert Hopoate also crossing the whitewash.

Hull KR had gone over through Dean Hadley but it ended up merely a consolation at the full-time whistle, Williams rubbing salt in the wound with a late drop goal and Toby King finishing things off with a try.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ashton completes his hat-trick after James Bentley relieves the pressure with a crucial interception, before the Warrington winger races through to extend their lead Ashton completes his hat-trick after James Bentley relieves the pressure with a crucial interception, before the Warrington winger races through to extend their lead

Warrington will head to play Leeds on Friday September 25, with kick-off at 8pm live on Sky Sports as they compete for a spot in the Grand Final. Wigan Warriors will then host Wakefield Trinity on Saturday September 26, with kick-off at 5.30pm on Sky Sports, as they bid to complete the final two.

Warrington a step closer to Grand Final as Peters era comes to close

After an early repeat set, it was not long until some eyes-up rugby saw Warrington get the first points on the board. Williams had some incredible vision to send the grubber kick through and while Burgess collected it, he half fumbled, which allowed Currie to collect and go in under the sticks.

Irwin converted and the home team were quickly 6-0 up, much to the delight of a packed-out Halliwell Jones Stadium.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Currie capitalises on Joe Burgess losing control near his own try line to give Warrington Wolves the perfect start against Hull KR Ben Currie capitalises on Joe Burgess losing control near his own try line to give Warrington Wolves the perfect start against Hull KR

Ill-discipline was costing the Robins and, once again, Warrington turned that into points. Irwin slotted over the penalty for offside and an eight-point lead was in place within 15 minutes.

Tries were then denied for both sides in corner-flying finishes from Ashton and Burgess that looked sublime, but neither winger could get the ball down before being bulldozed into touch.

With four minutes left of the half, the Robins scored a sensational full-length effort started off by a pass from Jack Broadbent to Mourgue who used his step and raced 70 metres before finding Burgess who did the rest. Mourgue converted and there were just two points in it.

That closeness did not last for long, as on the stroke of half-time, Kelepi Tanginoa broke through and found Ashton who used his pace to dive in for his 100th Super League try. Irwin's conversion attempt hit the post, so Warrington walked in with a 12-6 lead after 40 minutes of enthralling rugby league.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Burgess finishes a superb length-of-the-field Hull KR move after Arthur Mourgue slices through the Warrington defence Burgess finishes a superb length-of-the-field Hull KR move after Arthur Mourgue slices through the Warrington defence

The key moment of the game came three minutes into the second half when a suspected punch from Hiku on Williams resulted in a red card. There was not much force in it but he hit the Warrington captain's face and left the Robins with 12 for the remainder.

Warrington made sure to immediately capitalise from it as they sent it out wide for Ashton to finish off his second try. It looked to be a forward pass but was given and so the Wolves were 16-6 up with 35 minutes remaining.

Despite being a player down, Hull KR would not give up and got their reward in the 53rd minute when a breakaway from Burgess was eventually finished by Hadley barrelling over from close range. Mourgue converted to bring the score to 16-12 and we had a game on our hands.

The tension had reached a new level inside Warrington's home but it was alleviated with just a quarter to go. James Bentley came up with a massive interception and Ashton followed to pick up from the play the ball and race away for his hat-trick.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

That felt like the crucial score and Warrington then took control as Hopoate went in with a brilliant dive at the corner and Irwin came through clutch for a 16-point lead.

Just to rub salt in the wound, Williams sent over the one-pointer and, with a minute on the clock, King walked through and Irwin wrapped up the 35-12 victory and a spot in the semi-finals.

In the away end, there was extended applause for outgoing head coach Peters and the dynasty he has built. Burgess, meanwhile, celebrated on the pitch with his family as he continues his quest to do something just as monumental for Warrington.

Peters: Discipline cost us | Burgess: We should have closed out game earlier

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Willie Peters reflects emotionally on his four years at Hull KR after his final game in charge, before leaving to become the inaugural head coach of NRL newcomers PNG Chiefs Willie Peters reflects emotionally on his four years at Hull KR after his final game in charge, before leaving to become the inaugural head coach of NRL newcomers PNG Chiefs

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters, speaking to Sky Sports:

"Discipline has cost us a lot this year, and unfortunately it did again tonight, but I can't fault the players. I'm really proud of them. They kept fighting until the end.

"Warrington played really well and have been a very good team all year. I wish them all the best, but I'm really, really proud of this group and what they've achieved over the last four years. We've made a lot of beautiful memories.

"When you're down to 12 men it makes things difficult, but we still put ourselves in the game. We scored at the other end, went two points ahead and then, against the run of play, they scored.

"Fatigue always creeps in and it did towards the back end of the game. Peta has been great for us for three years. What he did was probably the wrong thing, but he's been outstanding for me throughout that time."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess, speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm proud of the group. It was a strange game, but we're pleased to come through and get another week together, which is what we came for. In the first half we felt really dominant and were disappointed with the scoreline.

"We left two or three tries out there and probably a couple more in the second half. We've just got to understand how important precision is because, over the course of a game, those moments add up. We could have finished the game much earlier."

Sports.title: Hits and misses: Spurs hit self-destruct again as Arsenal prove imperfect
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa

This Tottenham team are not a lost cause. But being bad in both boxes is a footballing nightmare. And that is where Spurs find themselves right now. Five games, no wins. And back in the relegation zone.

They are wasteful in front of goal and then seemingly determined to self-destruct at the other end. Sloppy passes, poor decisions, defensive lapses - gifts being handed out to the opposition.

And Roberto De Zerbi cut a frustrated figure. He called the defending for Aston Villa's second goal "unacceptable".

You could feel the anger bubbling underneath him in his post-match press conference. The most damning admission? He didn't even speak to his players after the defeat. That tells you plenty.

What was there to say? The same mistakes keep appearing. The same problems keep costing Spurs. And now, just when the manager needs his players on the training pitch to put it right, the international break arrives. Some of them won't see De Zerbi again for more than two weeks.

This isn't a lost season. There is too much talent in this Tottenham squad for that. But talent means very little if you keep shooting yourself in the foot. Top teams don't behave like this.

And if De Zerbi doesn't get that habit out of them quickly, this project is going to become another season of humiliation.

Lewis Jones

Image: Nicolas Jackson fires Aston Villa into a 2-0 lead at Spurs

Nicolas Jackson absolutely tormented Tottenham with a brilliant mixture of silky touches and bruising physicality. He gave Spurs' centre-backs no peace, constantly offering an out-ball, protecting possession and bringing those around him into the game.

It was the kind of performance that reminded you why Chelsea saw so much in him. Jackson doesn't always get the goals his all-round game perhaps deserves, but that can sometimes disguise just how valuable he is to the team. When he is playing with this confidence, everything seems to click. The midfielders have someone to find. The wide players have someone to combine with. Runners have space to attack.

It was a proper centre-forward's performance that included the game's key goal, which doubled Villa's lead.

It was a demonstration to Tottenham of exactly what they are missing through the middle.

Lewis Jones

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brighton and Arsenal

Arsenal lost 3-0 but it should have been six. Brighton missed three big chances to add to their hefty tally. We've rarely seen this from Mikel Arteta's team.

The last time Arsenal conceded three goals in a Premier League away game was in December 2023, and the Gunners even won that game at Luton 4-3. The last time they lost by a three-goal margin was May 2023, coincidentally against Brighton.

Arsenal went the entire of 2024, 2025 and most of 2026 without doing what they did at Brighton. It was uncharacteristic display, particularly on the road - where Arsenal have accumulated more away points than any other team in the last five years.

Arteta knew that Arsenal were in trouble right from the first throw-in in the game. And the way in which Arsenal were second-best from that moment to the 95th minute, this was clearly a bad day at the office, but not part of a wider problem.

Arteta was keen to call for perspective after the game: Arsenal have won every other match this season after staggering so many late arrivals from the World Cup and suffering a fair few injuries in defence.

The last time Arsenal lost in this manner was the 2026 Carabao Cup final - after which, the tactical template of 'how to beat Arsenal' then spilled into a FA Cup exit, a loss to Bournemouth and then that defeat at Manchester City which temporarily turned the title race tide.

The lengthy international break will help, but Arsenal need to make sure this Brighton blip doesn't become wobble.

Sam Blitz

Brighton have started the season in electric fashion. They are comfortably the Premier League's top scorers, who have added goals to the third-best defence in the league from last season.

Interestingly, all under Fabian Hurzeler, they have won a game against the reigning champions three seasons in a row. But when they beat Man City and Liverpool in previous years, those two clubs were already in freefall. Stopping Arsenal in their full flow makes this Brighton win the best out of the three.

What makes Brighton unique is how they respond to challenges? Lose Carlos Baleba? Chema Andres will arrive and step up. Danny Welbeck leaves and Georginio Rutter is out? Babis Kostoulas will score to get you wins over United and Arsenal.

Jack Hinshelwood is injured? Pascal Gross will get you seven goal contributions in five games. "He's like a fine wine," said Hurzeler about the German after the game. The same goes for his team. They just keep getting better and better.

Sam Blitz

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Everton and Ipswich Town

There is something quite endearing about Everton under David Moyes. After all the hardships of the transfer window, with the smallest squad in the division, they continue to overachieve. VAR even tried to undermine their victory over Ipswich, but they rallied to make sure it didn't matter.

Everton remain unbeaten in their opening seven games across all competitions, complete with five clean sheets. When asked if working with a small squad has actually been to his advantage, Moyes said: "We're trying to make it that way."

Their 21 shots against Ipswich were their most in a Premier League game at Hill Dickinson Stadium, but Moyes still sees plenty to improve on. "I am ratting the players like you wouldn't believe," he added. "Why are we not scoring more?"

Thierno Barry was denied what most would consider a legitimate goal by VAR, but Everton were also responsible for squandering four big chances themselves. That level of profligacy will come back to bite in certain games. And yet, you cannot help but be impressed by the way Moyes has maximised the finite tools at his disposal.

His managerial nous can take Everton further than their recruitment limitations suggested was possible.

Laura Hunter

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Newcastle United and Hull City

It was Newcastle's valiant defending that may have seen them over the line in their 2-1 victory against Hull, but it was their blistering first-half attack which proved the telling difference on the way to three points - especially that of Harvey Barnes.

Barnes provided two assists in just seven minutes, the earliest into a Premier League game a Newcastle player has set up mulitple goals, taking the record from Fabian Schar who managed the feat in nine minutes in that 6-1 demolition job of Tottenham in 2023.

The difference here was that Barnes was facing a resolute defence that had only conceded in one of their previous four Premier League games - not that that stopped the winger picking their locks twice in four minutes.

His deft inside through-ball for Joe Willock to lash home came just four minutes before slipping in a galloping Lewis Hall on the outside of the opponents' box - but he continued to provide Newcastle a creative spark throughout the 90 minutes, whipping in teasing crosses even when his side was up against it.

Barnes now has five goal contributions in seven games across all competitions for new boss Matthias Jaissle, but was still overlooked for Thomas Tuchel's England squad, missing out to Eberechi Eze, who has not started a Premier League game for Arsenal so far this campaign.



If the Englishman keeps producing game-defining performances like he has so far under Jaissle, it surely will not be long before he earns the trust of the other German manager he is eager to impress.

Noah Langford

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Nottingham Forest and Coventry

Coventry's last Premier League win before their 1-0 victory at Nottingham Forest on Saturday came 25 years ago when the Sky Blues beat Sunderland at home.

On that day in April 2001, there was no such thing as VAR, but on Coventry's return to the top flight, VAR was needed to get them over the line at the City Ground.

Had Igor Jesus' goal stood, it would have felt very cruel on Coventry, who were worth their victory.

They battled superbly, showed fantastic spirit and had moments of quality in attack capped off by Jay Dasilva's fine winner as goalkeeper Carl Rushworth assisted the goal.

There had been a fear Frank Lampard's side would become the basement boys after a pointless and goalless start to the season.

But on their fifth attempt, the Sky Blues showed they are Premier League material.

An away day win at the City Ground, however, is becoming far too regular an occurrence for Forest.

Among ever-present sides since the start of last season, only Tottenham have won fewer home games (3) and earned fewer home points (16) in the Premier League than Forest (4 wins, 21 points).

Forest boss Glasner believes the "heaviness of the past" is affecting the squad around home games, but this defeat was not for the want of trying.

Forest had 24 shots, their second most in a Premier League match since they returned to the division in 2022.

The upcoming three-week international break will leave Glasner searching for answers as to how to fix their home form and make their performances more clinical in front of goal.

Declan Olley

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brentford and Chelsea

For the first time this season, Chelsea were without their infamous front three of 'JP Morgan' due to Joao Pedro's injury.

Danny Welbeck started in the Brazilian's place and it was set up for the England international to do well. Brentford were Welbeck's favourite opponents in his career, with six goals in his nine previous matches against the Bees before Friday night.

But Chelsea weren't the same in attack. The new-formed attack of Welbeck, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers managed just one shot on target between them at the Gtech. They averaged three shots on target in each of their previous four league games.

Pedro is not just a goalscorer, he's a player who drops off the frontline to link up with others. He has just as managed goals as he has assist this season. Welbeck is less of a creator, more of a clinical scorer.

Xabi Alonso says Pedro's absence cannot be used as an excuse - but the Chelsea manager is surely hoping in private that he is back quickly after the international break.

Sam Blitz

Brentford's best buy of the transfer window may not be Mamadou Sangare after all. Jannik Schuster has announced himself to the Premier League after his £13m move from Red Bull Salzburg.

For all of Brentford's excellent attacking play - they scored three times, Igor Thiago got off the mark for the season and Kevin Schade's two assists rubberstamped his brilliant start to the season - it was in defence where they shone just as much. They are the first team to stop Chelsea scoring this season.

Schuster was a big part of that, with some outstanding defensive numbers earning the 20-year-old Player of the Match.

Image: Jannik Schuster impressed for Brentford vs Chelsea

His 12 clearances was twice as many as the next Brentford player, which is not bad given his first home Premier League start was up against a formidable and experienced opponents in Welbeck.

"I loved him from the second I saw him," said Keith Andrews after the win over Chelsea. "He's fearless, you could see his character from just watching clips. He's whole-hearted, he has personality and aggression. They way he truly plays, he loves defending."

Brentford have done it again.

Sam Blitz

Sports.title: Coventry seal first PL win in 25 years at Forest amid VAR controversy
Sports.content:
Coventry earned their first Premier League victory in 25 years after Jay Dasilva's winner and a controversial disallowed Nottingham Forest equaliser saw the promoted side win 1-0 at the City Ground.

Frank Lampard's side needed a late VAR intervention to end their long wait for victory after Forest substitute Igor Jesus saw an 86th-minute equaliser ruled out.

Referee Jarred Gillett was sent to the pitchside monitor, where he adjudged Jesus had fouled Caleb Yirenkyi before finishing from close range inside the area.

Questioned on the incident, Lampard told Sky Sports: "As you see on the replay, he has that little step on him which puts him off balance, and it's a foul...I think that's VAR reaching the right decision."

It was the second goal Forest have had disallowed at home by VAR this season after Neco Williams had a goal chalked off in the 0-0 draw against Tottenham. and Oliver Glasner said afterwards: "I don't want to talk about it, to be honest. The referee decided, but of course it's a bit of deja-vu."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Dasilva scores Coventry's winner

The latest controversial call meant Dasilva's 55th-minute goal, assisted by goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, ended the Sky Blues' pointless and goalless start to the season.

The visitors also needed a superb 76th-minute Bobby Thomas goalline clearance to deny Jesus an equaliser.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Coventry's Bobby Thomas clears a shot from Jesus

Forest's defeat means Glasner's side are yet to score or win at home in any competition this season, while they have won just once in the league at the City Ground since December last year.

Forest had 14 shots in the first half but were undone just 10 minutes after half-time as Rushworth's pinpoint long ball found Dasilva, who took a superb touch to beat Daniel Munoz before firing coolly beyond Matz Sels.

Dasilva's first goal in 127 Coventry appearances moves the Sky Blues off the foot of the table and inside the relegation zone only on goal difference, while Forest sit 12th.

Redknapp: Coventry showed they can do it in PL

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp:

"It's been a really hard start for them [Coventry], in terms of the teams they've had to play. But there were signs where they thought, 'we can compete at this level'.

"It was so important to get this win. I'm pleased for the players, the fans and obviously for Frank Lampard.

"They've done such a great job getting here, and now you want to make it count. You want to get rid of that inferiority complex. Can we handle the occasion and the Premier League? They showed that.

"They defended really well, looked dangerous on the break with some big performances."

Lampard: We have to keep feet on ground

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Frank Lampard reacts to Coventry's win over Nottingham Forest in the Premier League - marking the club's first victory in the top flight for 25 years

Coventry boss Frank Lampard speaking at his post-match press conference:

"We have to keep our feet on the ground because it's one win, and we've felt how ruthless the league is already.

"We've had two of the toughest games on paper, probably in (Manchester) City and Arsenal, but it doesn't matter.

"The points still said zero after four games, and that hurts. So I think going into a break, yeah, for sure, for everyone to have a bit of rest, to feel good about it.

"You know that's the starting point, so they can use that.

"Every win is a relief, no matter what. I mean, especially in our position, because you sit at the bottom of the table, you want to win because you don't like to look at it.

"But even when you're top of the Championship last year, there's a version of a relief for the manager, anyway."

Glasner: Defeat is a result of 'heaviness from the past'

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner speaking at his post-match press conference:

"For me, being very honest, I felt for the first time the heaviness of the past. The players were very quiet before the game.

"I just saw and felt that everybody, let's say, with a red shirt, got nervous today, and I think this is, for me now, and I'm still in the process of understanding the players, understanding Forest, maybe the biggest part of what we have to get under control, not to feel this pressure.

"Today we felt, 'ah, we have to win it now'. We play a promoted team at home. We have to win.

"We have to win, and we all know then some things don't work, and that's how I analyse the game.

"So, for me, the biggest problem was not the football skill; it was more the mental side, and that's why it's pretty clear now players need support here."

The key moments from the City Ground

1: FOREST SHOT ON TARGET! James McAtee hits a controlled, powerful volley which is straight at Rushworth.

16: COVENTRY SHOT ON TARGET! Lovely interplay between the Coventry forwards leads to Brandon Thomas-Asante having a low shot which is easily saved by Sels.

20: FOREST SHOT ON TARGET! Williams has a powerful drive from outside the box which is straight at Rushworth.

HALF-TIME: There were 20 shots in the first half - the most attempts in the first half of a Premier League game with no goals since Brentford vs Liverpool (24) in January 2025.

55: COVENTRY GOAL! The visitors score their first league goal of the season as Rushworth finds Dasilva, who takes one touch before producing a composed finish.

76: OFF THE LINE! Thomas superbly hooks away Jesus' chipped effort off the line.

86: FOREST SCORE BUT VAR DISALLOWS IT! Jesus pounces as Yirenkyi fails to clear, but VAR spots that Jesus had made contact on the Coventry midfielder before scoring and the goal is disallowed.

Sports.title: Portsmouth hit back to hold Blackburn
Sports.content:
Colby Bishop scored a fortuitous late leveller as Portsmouth drew 2-2 with Blackburn at Fratton Park.

John Mousinho made three changes from Pompey's dour 0-0 draw at Charlton with Bishop among those making way.

Tony Mowbray was also forced into making a change from Blackburn's win against Millwall as Yuri Ribeiro missed out with a hamstring issue and Harry Pickering came in.

The visitors started the brighter and Sam Morsy fed the ball through to captain Todd Cantwell inside the box, forcing the game's first corner via a deflected shot aimed point-blank at Daniel Bielica.

It was Pompey though who opened the scoring when Zak Swanson volleyed home past Rovers keeper Balazs Toth after Tyrese Shade's cross from the left was only half-cleared by Sean McLoughlin.

Image: Ryoya Morishita celebrates after scoring for Blackburn against Portsmouth

That lead lasted just seven minutes until Oladapo Afolayan netted his third goal in two games by converting a right-footed strike into the near post, making the most of a chipped ball played to him from the centre of the field by Pickering.

Bielica was forced into action again to scramble away Afolayan's flick-on from close range and then straight down the other end, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen scuffed an effort high and wide after a well-worked move which began with the receiving of a 40-yard diagonal switch from Madiodio Dia.

Abu Kamara was denied a first goal back in Pompey colours when Pickering timed a sliding challenge inside the penalty area well to clear the danger as the winger was preparing to shoot.

Home captain Marlon Pack received the game's first yellow card following a tackle in midfield on Rovers goalscorer Afolayan five minutes before the interval.

After surviving 10 minutes of Pompey dominance in the opening stages of the second half, Rovers took the lead for the first time in the game through Ryoya Morishita's drilled effort into the far corner, set up by Afolayan.

Mousinho's misery with injuries was further compounded by the forced withdrawal of Conor Shaughnessy, who pulled up unchallenged and had to be replaced after an hour.

His side did however claw their way back into the game when substitute Bishop inadvertently deflected in Kavuma-McQueen's right-footed effort after the Chelsea loanee did superbly to keep the opportunity alive for the hosts

Pompey had chances to snatch a third through Kamara and Bishop but were unable to find that late winner as the points were shared.

Both Mousinho and Mowbray will be relatively satisfied to head into the first international break of the season with a draw.

The managers

Portsmouth's John Mousinho:

"It was a frustrating afternoon with the fact we went a goal up, controlled the game but didn't win.

"We did everything but put the ball in the back of the net and were annoyed by the way we conceded the second goal.

"Maybe we had a bit of luck with our equaliser but we definitely could have won on the balance of chances.

"We put in a lot of effort but that is the bare minimum. We needed a bit more quality at times, in both boxes."

Blackburn's Tony Mowbray:

"We'll put the point in the bag and move on to the next game.

"There is a bit of frustration around it, really, to get ourselves in front. We should have been able to see that game out but unfortunately we didn't.

"At our best and in moments, we look like a really good football team, and yet I felt we probably showed them too much respect today, allowed them to build into our attacking third too easily.

"I am disappointed and frustrated, but it's a point away at Portsmouth, which is never an easy place to come to, with the atmosphere that the supporters create.

"I feel we have to get better. It wasn't a top performance from us, slightly below par, I think.

"We have to have better control. You've talked about Portsmouth. I feel we should be coming here and controlling a huge part of this game and get to a point where we believe that we're going to win.

"We should win and we are disappointed, but more frustrated today that we couldn't get to the performance level.

"I think we were below par today and that's probably down to them, but I think we should have managed the game better."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: The Blaze beat Hampshire in final-ball thriller to secure domestic treble
Sports.content:
The Blaze secured a domestic treble by edging a last-ball thriller with Hampshire to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup women’s competition.

The Trent Bridge-based side had already lifted the Vitality Blast and Vitality T20 County Cup but were forced to dig deep after needing 17 from the last two overs and then two off the final ball.



Emma Jones was the hero with an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls and scored the winning runs - after Tammy Beaumont and Georgia Elwiss had scored half-centuries in the chase of 252.

Earlier, Lucy Higham had taken 4-49 to help restrict Hampshire - who were also losing finalists in 2025 - to 251, with Ella McCaughan and Freya Kemp whacking fifties in vein.



The Blaze won the toss and, through the miserliness of Grace Ballinger and Charley Phillips, only allowed 11 runs in the first five overs.



But Hampshire's opening pair of the super-in-form Maia Bouchier and McCaughan slowly began to turn the tide in their direction with an 84-run stand.



McCaughan confidently pinged the ball around for her first fifty since June.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Women's Vitality Blast final at The Oval as Beaumont and Sarah Bryce powered The Blaze to a 10-wicket win over Durham

Bouchier, who was dropped on a duck, could not make it three centuries in a row when she holed out to long-on before Georgia Adams slapped straight to mid-off shortly afterwards - both to Higham.



The hosts kicked back as McCaughan and Kemp dominated the middle overs with a 67-run stand and were 166-2 in the 32nd over. But The Blaze used their final nous to pull things back.



Higham added wickets three and four of the afternoon by having Kemp stumped and Naomi Dattani caught brilliantly by Kirstie Gordon at mid-on.



The spinner has taken 14 wickets in eight matches since her return from The Hundred - with this 4-49, her third four-for in that period.



Pacer Phillips dismissed Rhianna Southby, Abi Norgrove and Amanda-Jade Wellington in three overs in a row, as Hampshire slumped and could only reach 251.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The pick of the action from Emirates Old Trafford as England thumped Sri Lanka by eight wickets to complete a 3-0 T20 series sweep and move back top of the world rankings

In response, Sarah Bryce and Beaumont made mincemeat of the bowlers for 15 overs, as they strode towards the target.



The pair put on 95 with relative ease, and then Wellington spun things by seeing off both Bryce sisters in an over - Sarah was caught at deep square before Kathryn was superbly caught at slip.



Beaumont, with the help of Elwiss, kept things ticking, although the former England opener lived a charmed life - she was dropped three times and also survived a stumping chance.



Her luck ran out, having scored her fifth half-century of the campaign, when she was lbw to Wellington - sparking three wickets to fall in 26 balls.



And with 30 still needed, Gordon was caught. It meant there was 17 required from the last two overs, but Jones took the sting out of things.



A ridiculous reverse pull and a straight drive both went to the boundary, and despite a run out with the third ball, Jones took her side to victory with a swept four off the final ball of a nerve-filled match.

Sports.title: Brighton demolish champions Arsenal 3-0 to mark anniversary in style
Sports.content:
So much for the new Invincibles. Arsenal were brought back down to earth with a shuddering bump by a scintillating display from Brighton as Fabian Hürzeler’s vibrant side celebrated the club’s 125th anniversary in style.

The special edition shirts they wore to mark the occasion will end up being collector’s items after the Premier League champions were ripped apart. Arsenal were attempting to record an eighth successive victory in all competitions to start the new campaign for the first time since 1903 when they were still known as Woolwich Arsenal.

Instead, it is Brighton – inspired by first-half goals from the veteran stand-in captain, Pascal Gross, and the exciting teenager Charalampos Kostoulas – who find themselves in third place, two points behind Arsenal. New signing Chema Andrés made the points safe from a corner 12 minutes into the second half. That meant Arsenal conceded three goals for the first time since December 2023 in all competitions and Mikel Arteta will be most concerned that it could easily have been more against the division’s top scorers, 16 in five games.

The home supporters waved blue and white flags before kick-off as the players swapped their usual kits for a deep blue limited edition shirt that was inspired by their first season in Southern League Division Two in 1901. That has caused controversy among fans after originally being listed on sale for £150 in a package that included a letter of authenticity from the club owner, Tony Bloom, and a keyring. Given this is the only time they will wear it, those who shelled out will be pleased they did now.

What has made Brighton’s goalscoring exploits so impressive is that they have managed it almost completely without their first-choice attack due to injury, while last year’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, was sold to Chelsea in the summer. Georginio Rutter returned as a late substitute, but the damage had already been inflicted by then thanks to Gross and Kostoulas.

Jurriën Timber looked leggy on his first start since March and Bruno Guimarães was disappointing on his first Premier League start for Arsenal. Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy and drive in midfield was sorely missed in the week he was recalled to the England squad.

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross fires home Brighton’s first goal against Arsenal. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

From the first whistle, Kostoulas – signed last summer for £30m – led Brighton’s fearsome press that provoked Arsenal into a number of uncharacteristic errors, including a misplaced pass from Guimarães that forced David Raya to tip a deflected effort from the 19-year-old around the post. Raya was also guilty of donating possession to the lively Yasin Ayari in a dangerous position. Arsenal and Arteta looked rattled for the first time this season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Christos Tzolis could not take a rare opportunity on the break after being picked out by Bukayo Saka and they were made to pay for it just after the half-hour mark. Perhaps wary of the unmarked Ayari to their left, Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori were slow to challenge Gross when he received the ball on the edge of Arsenal’s area from Kostoulas and the veteran picked his spot perfectly off the inside of the post.

Ayari came close to doubling the lead five minutes before half-time when he fired into the side-netting before Kostoulas did. Saka had just spurned a great chance to equalise after being set up by Martin Ødegaard and once again Gabriel was guilty of ball watching as the Greek striker thumped the ball past Raya from 25 yards.

Arteta immediately sent out Max Dowman, who scored two goals against Ipswich in midweek, to warm up. He must have been tempted to throw the 16-year-old on at the start of the second half as Kostoulas went close again for Brighton.

It was too late once Andrés nodded in at the far post from a pinpoint Gross corner. “Are you Tottenham in disguise?” sang the delighted Brighton fans.

Arteta introduced Dowman with 10 minutes remaining as he emptied his bench. But having been knocked off the top of the Premier League on goal difference courtesy of this heavy loss, there will be plenty of soul-searching during the three-week international break for the Arsenal manager.

Sports.title: De Zerbi rips into Spurs players after Villa defeat: ‘Disappointed, sad and frustrated’
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi tore into his failing Tottenham team after their 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa, saying “we can’t lose the game in this way”. The Italian headed straight down the tunnel at full time, but was once again forced to endure boos as Tottenham went into the three-week international break without a Premier League victory to their name and just two points on the board.

De Zerbi criticised his team’s mentality, but also the physical condition of his players, and said the substitute Mohammed Kudus had disrupted the balance of his team.

“I am very disappointed, sad and frustrated for the performance,” De Zerbi said. “We can’t lose the game in this way, we can’t concede the second goal, we can’t lose balance just because we are losing. I spoke with our four attackers in minute 51, I asked them to use their head, all second half I was telling people to be calm. But the second goal was incredible.”

Jackson scored in the 67th minute after latching on to a long kick by the impressive Zion Suzuki. De Zerbi said his players had been prepped to deal with the Villa goalkeeper’s clearances, but had switched off.

“We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86% more long balls than last season and we spoke in many meetings about it,” De Zerbi said. “Now we have to explain another game like [the home defeat against] Newcastle where we played the first half well, got to 60 minutes OK, and then we lose.”

Quick Guide How do I 

With players now heading out to play for their national sides, De Zerbi said he had left them with no parting message. “I didn’t speak with the players because I didn’t want to say anything. The players who go with the national team have to play and work. For sure we have to work more because I didn’t like the finish to this game. We can’t say everything is bad, but it is not enough.”

For Unai Emery, a first Premier League victory of the season a reminder to his players of the style of play that has resulted in success for Villa in recent seasons. “The players did well because they believed,” he said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We needed to build a team that could play in this way, could defend with resilience and playing with passion when our opponents were attacking. We needed defenders, we needed the keeper, we needed everyone committed in that direction. We needed to feel strong first, then we could try to play with our structure and our ability. This is the competitive way.”

Sports.title: Holmberg rescues point for Arsenal but Manchester United off the mark in WSL
Sports.content:
Arsenal were mightily relieved as a 95th-minute Smilla Holmberg volley rescued a point at home to a much-improved Manchester United side, but the draw will not be enough to eradicate concerns about how far behind the leaders Manchester City Renée Slegers’ team are slipping already and how frequently they seem to struggle to break down a low block.

A defiant Manchester United stunned the north Londoners as Eva Olid’s side claimed the first point of her tenure with a performance that defied all of the pre-match scripts, but it was very nearly a victory, had it not been for Holmberg’s last-gasp back-post finish from Leah Williamson’s deep, diagonal ball into the box, which finally broke the visitors’ stubborn resistance.

Widely criticised for their dismal displays in their opening two defeats against London City Lionesses and Chelsea, Manchester United were heavily tipped to struggle again at the Emirates but an encouraging defensive effort and an against-the-run-of-play Julia Zigiotti Olme strike gave them a precious lead in a display that will buy the former Hearts manager Olid plenty of time to continue working on her style on the training ground and quieten those doubting her.

Instead it will be Arsenal now facing scrutiny as they failed to win at home for a second straight game and slipped four points behind the defending champions, Manchester City, after just three rounds of fixtures. Last term, Manchester City dropped points in only four games and the early-season leaders have a 100% record so far. Arsenal’s next two WSL games are away to Chelsea and Manchester City.

“It’s not ideal, it’s not what we wanted at all, four lost points,” Slegers admitted, reflected on consecutive home draws, but she added: “It’s round three in the WSL, there are a lot of games left to play. Let’s see in May, how it ends. Not converting dominance into wins, that’s something we have to look at. We believe in the quality of the squad. When that starts clicking, it’s going to be really good.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Julia Zigiotti Olme celebrates scoring against Arsenal. Photograph: Paul Harding/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

In truth, this was a result that Arsenal could ill-afford, especially after last weekend’s goalless draw at home to the newly promoted side Crystal Palace, where the north Londoners were surprisingly wasteful in the final third. Slegers’ team had scored just one goal from 43 shots across their opening two league fixtures. Surely, therefore, a home match against a side who conceded five goals last time out was the perfect opportunity to banish any concerns of a lack of clinical quality in the final third? Think again.

The hosts did create good openings and looked to have control of the midfield. Their winger Lisa Baum shot straight at Phallon Tullis-Joyce early on and was providing dangerous crosses from the left. Mariona Caldentey also went close, curling just wide and Tullis-Joyce made a fine save to keep out Stina Blackstenius’ header. Nevertheless, it had been United’s Elisabeth Terland who went closest in the first half, being thwarted by two excellent Misa Rodríguez saves in quick succession.

View image in fullscreen Phallon Tullis-Joyce leaping up to make a crucial save to keep Arsenal at bay. Photograph: Nina Farooqi/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

Arsenal stepped up the pressure after half-time but Georgia Stanway – one of Arsenal’s better performers for the rest of the game – made a costly error as she tried to play a simple pass back towards the centre-back Steph Catley that carelessly rolled the ball into the path of Zigiotti Olme instead. The grateful Manchester United midfielder confidently stepped the ball around Catley and slotted through the legs of Rodríguez. The Emirates was astonished. The United bench, jubilant.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

From then on, it was ‘backs to the wall’ for the visitors, much like it was during the majority of this fixture last term, which ended goalless. Tullis-Joyce dived low and strong to keep out a Cailtin Foord effort and United battled well to clear the danger from several set pieces as the home side grew increasingly frustrated. The crowd eventually erupted as the substitute Holmberg earned them a point and Manchester United’s players fell to their knees.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Chelsea's Potter and Malard sink Birmingham Show Chelsea and London City Lionesses climbed the Women’s Super League table with respective victories over Birmingham and Charlton. After thumping Manchester United 5-0 last weekend, Chelsea won again as Lexi Potter and Melvine Malard secured a 2-0 win. Potter found the roof of the net in the eighth minute (the celebrations pictured above) and in the 71st minute the France star Malard made a quick impact from the bench with her first goal at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea moved up to second and with their goal difference were likely to stay there. London City lost 2-1 to West Ham last time out but impressed in a 4-1 triumph at promoted Charlton. Isobel Goodwin’s double had London City two goals ahead after 15 minutes and, despite Jodie Hutton halving the deficit in the 39th minute with a fine finish, Jana Fernández restored their advantage before half-time. The German forward Nicole Anyomi made sure the outcome was no longer in doubt with the Lionesses’ fourth after 76 minutes. They sit third, a point behind Chelsea. Press Association Photograph: Yaroslav Dunka/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Olid was pleased with their display, though, explaining: “After losing 5-0, the focus this week was the defensive shape, because I think the attack will come. Implementing a new style of play needs time. But the effort, the hard work, the intensity, that can never be missing. It was so important to see that today. That is the minimum. Now, from here, little-by-little, we will improve the attacking style.”

Sports.title: Coventry delight in Jay Dasilva winner but ruled-out goal riles Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
No, but seriously. Maybe Frank Lampard and Coventry can achieve Premier League survival. The club’s first top-division win since April 2001 was celebrated rapturously, victory an object lesson in unsettling opponents for whom confidence can waver. Jay Dasilva’s excellent goal was built on the foundations laid by a battling defensive performance that must be replicated on a weekly basis. Coventry, dogged throughout, blunted Nottingham Forest’s creativity, though could thank a late video assistant referee call that enraged the City Ground crowd.

Lampard declared, with his broadest grin: “I feel great, I feel amazing.” Next, as is his way, back to serious business. “The reality in football is you have to fight for it, you have to work for it, you have to have organisation.”

Coventry’s troubled start to the season had revived doubts in his capabilities as a Premier League manager and far too many echoes of a quarter century in the wilderness. Whatever happens, their fans, under the weakening, early-evening sun, were determined to enjoy themselves. Even if it’s for a single season, why not make the most of things? “Something we have to build on and not get too carried away,” said Bobby Thomas, having personified that rearguard effort.

“We are a team with a lot of players having their first stint in Premier League football,” said Lampard. “Not everyone is a Wayne Rooney or a superstar that can just own it.”

Forest’s home league record in 2026 continues to be wretched: only Burnley, in April, have left in defeat. The previous week’s victory at Aston Villa offered further confirmation of Morgan Gibbs-White’s importance to Forest, as if it were needed. He remains ignored by Thomas Tuchel despite verifiable claims of being the most in-form English No 10 around, only Pascal Gross creating more chances in the Premier League this season, though like his team as a whole, Gibbs-White is doing his best work away from West Bridgford. Forest hit 26 shots on Coventry’s goal, just three on target.

View image in fullscreen Jay Dasilva fires home Coventry’s 55th-minute winner. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

“We struggled with scoring,” was Oliver Glasner’s simple diagnosis. “Today was the first time I could feel the heaviness of the past, it was very quiet in the dressing room. When we conceded the goal, everyone was nervous, the entire ground was nervous and I think the reason is last year.”

An early deft header to Liam Delap and a cogent flick to James McAtee had suggested Gibbs-White was in the mood but Forest never found the momentum to crack Coventry’s defensive shield. McAtee’s talents have never quite found their position but playing deeper as Gibbs-White’s creative partner has suited him. However, the duo were far less in tune than the previous week. Delap has shown signs of being the player glimpsed at Ipswich but was another lost in heavy traffic, Forest reduced to potshots such as his snapshot wide.

Quick Guide Nottingham Forest 0-1 Coventry key facts Show • Coventry earned their first Premier League victory of the season – it’s their 100th win in the competition overall, and first since April 2001 (1-0 v Sunderland). • Jay Dasilva scored Coventry’s first Premier League goal of the season. Assisted by Carl Rushworth, it’s just the second time a team’s first goal in a campaign has been assisted by a goalkeeper, after Peter Schmeichel for Manchester United in 1992-93. • Nottingham Forest have failed to score in their first three home games in a league campaign for the first time in their history. Opta Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Coventry’s kick-off for the second half saw their players line up in a formation resembling that for a rugby union dropout. It achieved little but previewed the long-ball tactics that brought about the breaking of their 25-year duck.

Loum Tchaouna, a half-time arrival, cutting inside to shoot, if too weakly to beat Matz Sels, might have served as a further warning to Forest, as within moments, Dasilva, showing admirable strength for someone of such diminutive dimensions and a beautiful first touch to beat Daniel Muñoz, blazed to a diagonal ball from his goalkeeper, Carl Rushworth. The finish was just as adept, the celebrations deafening. Coventry’s previous Premier League scorer had been Mustapha Hadji in a losing effort at Aston Villa that confirmed relegation.

View image in fullscreen The big screen shows Igor Jesus has been deemed to have fouled Caleb Yirenkyi on review. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

For an increasingly ragged Forest, Chris Wood, old reliable, was thrown on, as was Igor Jesus, with Delap pushed to the wings. If anything, that led to Forest losing their shape and poise further, even if chances came. Thomas dashed back to the goalline to clear a chip from Igor Jesus that had Rushworth beaten.

Igor Jesus did get the ball in the net, only for the video assistant referee to advise Jarred Gillett that Caleb Yirenkyi had been fouled, and the on-pitch official agreed. It looked harsh: Yirenkyi had fallen readily under minimal contact. “I was worried,” Lampard said.

A shrugging Glasner said: “The referee decided and we accept it, that’s it.” Forest fans have had more than their fill of video-assisted officiating. Their seething, guttural rage came by contrast to Coventry fans now able to savour the Premier League ride.

Sports.title: Zidane’s next move as France coach may reveal the wizard behind the curtain | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Even in his playing days, Zinedine Zidane seemed unknowable. As a manager, the sense of distance has only grown. He won three Champions Leagues with Real Madrid without ever giving a sense of what his idea of football looked like.

France are perhaps the most perplexing football country: a squad that teems with such talent that a B team would be serious contenders at a World Cup, that reached three major finals under Didier Deschamps with a sense of unfulfilment, a team that progressed but rarely entranced, or at least didn’t until this summer’s World Cup, when they attacked with gusto and ended up overrun in midfield by Spain.

On Friday, the two come together as Zidane, for the first time, leads France in their Nations League fixture against Turkey, an enigmatic coach leading a mercurial squad.

Zidane is one of five coaches to have won the Champions League on three or more occasions, ranking alongside Bob Paisley, Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique and behind only Carlo Ancelotti. He is the only manager to win three successive Champions Leagues and yet few would consider him one of the game’s elite coaches. In that spell he won one La Liga title.

He left five days after the third of those Champions League successes, vaguely citing the club’s need for change. Like so much else in his career, his motivations were opaque. But he returned the following March after the inglorious reign of Julen Lopetegui and Santi Solari’s attempt to pick up the pieces. He won another La Liga title in the two full seasons that followed.

How to assess a coach in the modern world? Two league titles in four full seasons. Three Champions Leagues in his first two and a half seasons. In another age, in another country, that would have marked Zidane as indisputably elite, but in Spain in the past decade? Domestically, his achievements feel about par.

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was viewed at Real Madrid as a head coach who let his star players like Ronaldo and Gareth Bale just be. Photograph: Matt West/BPI/Shutterstock

Madrid and Barcelona win everything, so for a Madrid coach to win half the league titles available is essentially what would be expected. But he lost eight of his first 100 games, a record. His side scored in a record 73 consecutive games. They won a joint-record 16 La Liga games in a row. They won a record 13 successive away games.

They are stats that seem unanswerable, but their accumulation has the opposite effect to that which might be expected. Zidane’s Madrid, in his first spell, were crushingly dominant. But were they dominant because of his genius or did he appear a genius because of their dominance? What comes to matter, then, is not the how many, but the how. Did Madrid win with dashing football of fitting elegance? To which the answer is, again, a shrug: they were fine.

Those three Champions League wins in a row, equally, offer surprisingly little evidence for Zidane’s greatness. Madrid have always had a tremendous capacity for achieving European success in the shadows, as though they are the default, the club that wins when nobody else is quite inspired enough to do so. Rarely has that been felt as acutely as in 2016, when they beat Roma and Wolfsburg, then edged by Manchester City on penalties in the semi-final thanks to a Fernando own goal before beating Atlético Madrid on penalties in an unmemorable final.

The following year was more impressive: the extra-time surge against Bayern and Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired demolitions of Napoli, Atlético and Juventus. But 2018 was a return to curiously ordinary success. Yes, Ronaldo and Luka Modrić were often brilliant, but there was also carelessness, notably in the quarter-final win against Juventus when they let a three-goal lead slip before a late penalty rescued them. Victory over Liverpool in the final came after a shoulder injury sustained by Mohamed Salah in a challenge with Sergio Ramos, a terrible error by a possibly injured Loris Karius and a Gareth Bale wonder goal.

View image in fullscreen Didier Deschamps was successful as head coach of France, but his side rarely captivated Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

It was hard to isolate any one moment in the success that could definitively be assigned to Zidane’s coaching genius. He didn’t create the midfield three of Casemiro, Modric and Toni Kroos. He didn’t find some new role for Ronaldo or Bale. Perhaps Zidane was some elite player whisperer, coaxing them to habitual greatness, but it was hard for an outsider to tell. Being Zidane, he was inscrutable, a cipher into which observers could read whatever message they wished.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Real Madrid coaches often run into a similar problem. They have great players. Great players do great things. Philosophies and structures always seem subservient to their talents. Ancelotti, like Zidane, has often been underappreciated, seen as somebody who essentially lets the players be. That is probably unfair and, even if it were not, perhaps that, too, is a skill. After all, plenty of coaches at Real Madrid have not been able to let the players express their innate superiority.

At the very least, it can be said that Zidane has an aura. Even those who accused him of being little more than a pair of hands clapping on the touchline must acknowledge that some hands are more authoritative than others. That may turn out to be an essential quality with France, a national team that became notorious between their two World Cup triumphs for ill-discipline, with the scandals of Seoul in 2002 and the strike at Knysna in 2010.

Whatever doubts there may be about whether Deschamps’s caution was counterproductive – until at the last, in that semi-final against Spain, he wasn’t cautious enough – over his 14 years in charge he prevented the sort of breakdowns of discipline that had undermined his predecessors, despite some extremely challenging situations.

Perhaps this is not such a troubled or troublesome France squad as some of the past decade have been, but that Zidane has taken the unusual step of banning the press from covering the arrival of players at their Clairefontaine base suggests he is eager to make a bid for control early.

His squad features a number of new faces. This is not continuity Deschamps. In the greater autonomy national coaches have compared with their club counterparts, perhaps, with France, the true nature of Zidane the coach will emerge and the great enigma will develop a face.

Sports.title: Everton hold off Ipswich thanks to Thierno Barry goal despite VAR controversy
Sports.content:
After the trials and tribulations of the transfer window, Everton can be content with fifth place, an unbeaten start and five clean sheets in seven games. There will also be relief, for Pro Ref as well as David Moyes, that another controversial call from a video assistant referee did not impede their progress against Ipswich.

Thierno Barry decided a close-fought contest with his fifth goal of the campaign. He should have had a sixth but an offside Brennan Johnson was adjudged to have impacted Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton’s ability to save a ball he made no attempt to save and was nowhere near saving. Unlike last weekend’s Manchester derby, however, referee Stuart Attwell’s decision would not prove decisive. The game turned in Everton’s favour minutes later when Abdul Fatawu received a second yellow card for diving but, having failed to kill off Gary O’Neil’s 10 men, they ended up hanging on. VAR was therefore spared Moyes’s wrath.

“They said it affected his ability to save it which I don’t think was the case,” said the Everton manager, far more relaxed than he would have been had Ipswich levelled late on. “It’s really difficult for referees, we understand that. Do I think we will get consistency from that decision through all the season on the same thing? I’ll be doubtful of that. There is no doubt Brennan was offside but did he really interfere, was the goalkeeper ever going to save it?”

O’Neil took a differing view, and also claimed his visitors controlled the game. That was stretching it. Everton were extremely careless in possession with the usually reliable Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Jarrad Branthwaite, James Garner and Harrison Armstrong among those responsible. But they created enough chances to have rendered Ipswich’s stirring finale irrelevant, 21 in total, though managed only two on target. “I am ratting the players like you wouldn’t believe,” added Moyes. “Why are we not scoring more? I think that’s one of the things we are missing from being a half-decent side.”

Johnson missed a gilt-edged chance from an Armstrong pass before Barry delivered an early lead with his strangest goal of the season. The striker reacted sharply to divert James Tarkowski’s 25-yard volley into the net after Walton and the lively Jack Clarke had cleared a cross from Dewsbury-Hall. The Ipswich keeper had Tarkowski’s shot covered only for Barry to leave him wrong-footed by chesting the ball into the opposite side of the goal. The striker clearly moved to play the ball with his chest, so gets the benefit of the doubt over his intention.

Fatawu was a persistent threat down Ipswich’s right flank, making his dismissal all the more galling for O’Neil as his team chased an equaliser. The Ghana international forced a fine save from Jordan Pickford after Everton made a hash of clearing his corner and attempted to beat the England goalkeeper from inside his own half. The long-range effort was drifting wide but Pickford, unawares, took no chances and scampered back to save. Fatawu should also have claimed an assist when floating a cross over the Everton defence to Leif Davis. The left-back, perhaps surprised to find himself onside and unmarked in front of goal, scuffed his shot badly wide of the far post.

View image in fullscreen Stuart Attwell shows Ipswich’s Abdul Fatawu (centre) a second yellow card for simulation. Photograph: Alex Dodd/Shutterstock

Ipswich started the second half on top with Pickford saving from Julio Enciso and Abdoul Ouattara in quick succession. But it was Everton who converted next when Barry rose between four static Ipswich players and headed Dewsbury-Hall’s corner in off the far post. Walton was nowhere near the ball and did not appeal any infringement by the offside Johnson. Referee Attwell, sent to the pitch-side monitor, infuriated the home crowd by disallowing the goal on the basis Johnson was offside and affecting the keeper’s ability to save the ball.

Fatawu foolishly helped Everton recover. Booked for hauling down Dewsbury-Hall in the first half, the winger invited a second yellow card when diving to win a free-kick against Garner. He became only the third player in the last six Premier League seasons to receive a second yellow card for simulation.

Everton had numerous chances against Ipswich’s ten men but Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall and Armstrong all miscued while Walton produced a fine save to deny impressive substitute Tyler Dibling. Their profligacy made for a nervy finale as the visitors piled forward in search of an equaliser. Branthwaite, launching himself in the way of Diop’s goal-bound shot, helped Everton over the line.

Sports.title: Newcastle back to winning ways as Willock and Hall end Hull’s unbeaten start
Sports.content:
Hull always knew, sooner or later, they would lose a Premier League game, but no one can say they did not do everything in their power to try to delay that inaugural top-tier defeat.

After conceding two goals in the opening seven minutes, Hull could easily have folded but they are made of sterner stuff than that. Tellingly, they also sensed the inherent fragility of a gifted, but injury-hit and extremely youthful Newcastle.

Once Matthias Jaissle was forced into a late switch to an unloved three at the back and Mohamed-Ali Cho narrowed the scoreline, the visitors assumed control and it almost seemed a minor miracle that Newcastle clung on for a morale-boosting victory.

“I’m very proud of how we played this game, especially the second half,” said Sergej Jakirovic. “We made mistakes in the first 10 minutes and Newcastle were clinical on the counterattack, but after that, I think we showed our mentality and our character. Over 90 minutes, we deserved a point. My team showed they will not be beaten easily.”

Jaissle had harsh words for his players after Monday’s 4-1 defeat at Leeds and it seemed they had the desired effect. Sure enough, Joe Willock swiftly lashed the ball beyond Konstantinos Tzolakis. Three minutes were on the clock and it was only the third goal Hull’s £20m Greece goalkeeper had conceded since arriving from Olympiakos.

It came after John Egan blocked Willock’s initial shot, but Hull’s subsequent failure to clear permitted Harvey Barnes to pick out the midfielder.

Four minutes later, Barnes was once again the creator as he exchanged passes with the excellent Lewis Hall before the left-back, recalled to the England squad on Friday, swept the crispest of shots low into the bottom-left corner. Significantly, it had all begun with Hall dispossessing Oli McBurnie deep in Newcastle’s half.

Tino Livramento, too, was included in Thomas Tuchel’s latest squad, but the right-back’s chances of joining up with England receded when an injury collected in training ruled him out here. Livramento was one of nine home absentees, but, undeterred, a youthful starting XI initially delighted in a spot of tiger taming.

As much as Hull struggled to second-guess the dynamic Willock and the impressive 18-year-old Sean Steur in the home midfield, they were not subdued entirely. Hull came close to reducing the deficit when Sorba Thomas almost turned in a Matt Crooks cross at the near post.

When, deep in first-half stoppage time, Thomas slipped before pulling the advancing Jacob Murphy back by an ankle, a penalty was awarded. Yoane Wissa stepped up, but his rather under-powered kick was saved by Tzolakis.
