Maximilian Beier’s 70th-minute winner secured Borussia Dortmund a 1-0 victory at Stuttgart as they moved to the top of the early Bundesliga table. Beier tapped in from Jobe Bellingham’s low cross to send Dortmund to the summit for the first time since May 2023, a run of 1,212 days since they threw away the title with a final-day home draw against Mainz.

View image in fullscreen Maximilian Beier (centre) celebrates with teammates after scoring Borussia Dortmund’s winner against VfB Stuttgart. Photograph: Ronald Wittek/EPA

The victory also marks the first time in a decade Dortmund have won their opening four league matches. “Sounds good to me,” Beier told Sky Germany. “We’ll take that.”

Earlier, Freiburg had missed a chance to return to the top of the Bundesliga after being held to a 2-2 draw at Eintracht Frankfurt. Bayern Munich’s ruthless 7-0 win over Union Berlin on Friday had put them top overnight.

Several new members of the Jürgen Klopp’s 44-man Germany squad shone on both sides in a see-sawing encounter. Frankfurt’s Younes Ebnoutalib finished off a lovely team move to score 10 minutes in, two days after a surprise first call-up.

Derry Scherhant, another of Klopp’s lesser-known new additions, levelled things up for Freiburg, but Jonathan Burkardt edged Frankfurt back in front. Scherhant created a second for Yuito Suzuki to grab Freiburg a point and leave them level with Bayern on 10 points.

Mohamed Salah scored a hat-trick and set up another ⁠goal as Trabzonspor thrashed Galatasaray 4-0, handing the ⁠defending champions their first defeat of the Turkish Super Lig season.

Salah opened ⁠the scoring in the fourth minute, running through from midfield and finishing calmly, ⁠before he turned provider to set up Noah ​Saviolo, who struck ‌from inside ‌the penalty area in the 39th. Salah added a ‌third in the 44th minute with a clinical finish from a Franculino Dju assist. He completed his ‌hat-trick in the 80th minute, running more than half the length of the ​pitch unchallenged to score with a trademark side-foot finish.

Galatasaray’s coach, Okan Buruk, was sent to the stands in the 71st minute while Lesley ⁠Ugochukwu was shown a red card in the ​87th. Trabzonspor are fifth in the table with 10 points from six games, three points behind Galatasaray.

Sports.title: Andros Townsend run over by pitch roller in freak accident while warming up
Sports.content:
Andros Townsend run over by pitch roller in freak accident while warming up

Andros Townsend avoided serious injury after being run over by a pitch roller as he warmed up at half-time in Thailand.

The former Tottenham star, who now plies his trade in the Far East, was training during the break when the vehicle was driven directly into him.

3 Townsend was ran over by a pitch roller as his shocked teammates looked on Credit: X

Townsend currently plays his football in the Thai Premier League for PT Prachuap, who signed him in the summer.

However, during just his third league match since joining, he found himself involved in an extremely bizarre moment.

What happened to Townsend?

At half-time of PT Prachuap's match against Pattani on Saturday, Townsend was warming up with his teammates.

But as he passed the ball around, a staff member at the stadium started to drive their pitch roller onto the surface.

And they ended up driving it directly into Townsend, who had jumped out of the area the players were training in to complete a flicked pass and accidentally stepped into its path.

The metal roller, which was driven extremely close to the training players, hit Townsend's legs, knocking him to the ground with some force and driving on top of him.

The ex-England international's teammates looked visibly shocked and concerned, rushing over to help out after the roller fortunately came to a stop before going any further than his hips.

Townsend, who somehow avoided injury in the shock incident, ended up playing just one minute of the match.

He had started his first two appearances in PT Prachuap, but was named as a substitute for their clash with Pattani.

His side ended up winning the game 3-0 - moving up to second place in the Thai Premier League.

3 Townsend was fortunate to avoid injury as the roller hit directly into his legs Credit: X

3 The ex-England winger was knocked to the ground and left pinned to the grass Credit: X

Townsend's time in Thailand

The 35-year-old has been playing in Thailand for over a year having first joined Kanchanaburi Power last summer.

He played 30 games for the top-flight side - scoring three goals and providing six assists altogether.

Kanchanaburi Power would go on to get relegated from the Thai Premier League though, leading to his exit.

Townsend departed and signed for PT Prachuap to remain at the top level, with Saturday's clash his third appearance.

His playing days are still ongoing, extending his professional career to 17 years after starting off at Spurs.

He played for Newcastle, Crystal Palace, Everton, Luton and another 12 clubs, making 291 Premier League appearances in total.

Sports.title: Liam Rosenior refuses to apologise after sparking heated on-pitch riot against former club
Sports.content:
Liam Rosenior refuses to apologise after sparking heated on-pitch riot against former club

Liam Rosenior has no regrets after celebrating in front of his former club Strasbourg's fans on Saturday.

Rosenior, who now manages Paris FC, sparked a brawl on the pitch after his new side beat his old one 2-1 in Ligue 1.



3 Rosenior wildly celebrated in front of the Strasbourg fans after his Paris FC side beat them 2-1 Credit: AFP

Paris moved up to third in the table as they continued their unbeaten start to the season with another victory.

The ex-Chelsea manager is enjoying his time in the French capital, but beating Strasbourg appears to be his highlight so far.

What did Liam Rosenior do to the Strasbourg fans?

After the full-time whistle, as the visiting players clapped the travelling supporters, Rosenior entered the pitch.



Footage showed him walking towards the away end, waving his arms and shouting in celebration in the fans' direction.

He beat his chest and flung his arm at the Strasbourg supporters, with their players then rushing over towards him.



Chaos then ensued, with a scuffle breaking out on the pitch and both teams flooding towards the clash to get involved.

Rosenior was eventually dragged away from the heated moment and turned to the Paris FC fans to celebrate with them.



What did Rosenior say about the incident?

The full-time reaction from Rosenior appeared to follow insults coming his way from the stands - and he cleared up the reasoning behind the flashpoint when asked about it post-match.

"I will say, the people in the club that know me know I've always been respectful," he told Ligue 1 Plus.

"I've always wanted the best for that football club. I still do want the best for that football club.

3 A brawl ensued after Rosenior celebrated in front of the away end at full time Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



"When I heard the chants... I understand French, I understand the context of the language. That's a step too far. There are a lot of things that have happened.

"It's a wonderful football club, it's a great city, it's a club with great tradition, I've always protected those traditions.

"So for me to celebrate in the way that I did was for many reasons."

He later added in his press conference: "A small part of the supporters, and I emphasise, a small part of them because Strasbourg is a fantastic club, were disrespectful.

"They insulted my family. My bench was very angry. So for me, celebrating like that, obviously it was a message.



"I won't say anything more about it."

3 Rosenior left Strasbourg for Chelsea in January and now he's back in France with Paris Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

When did Rosenior leave Strasbourg?

Rosenior spent 18 months as Strasbourg manager from 2024 through to the start of 2026, when he joined Chelsea.

The former Premier League defender left the Ligue 1 outfit to join the Blues to replace Enzo Maresca in the dugout.

He took charge of 63 games as Strasbourg boss, winning 32 of them and leading them to Europe for the first time in six years.



Unfortunately for him though, his stint at Chelsea would only last four months, losing ten of 23 games in the role.

Four months after his quick sacking at Stamford Bridge, Rosenior was appointed as Paris FC manager, returning to France.

And he's thrived since, winning three matches and drawing two in Ligue 1 since his appointment.

Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara tips Tottenham for relegation as Jason Cundy blocks him from storming out of studio
Sports.content:
Jamie O’Hara tips Tottenham for relegation as Jason Cundy blocks him from storming out of studio

Jamie O'Hara has finally answered Jason Cundy's all-important Tottenham question: "Are you going down?"

The former Spurs midfielder and fan has now admitted that he thinks his side could well end up being relegated this season.



3 O'Hara admitted that he thinks Spurs could go down after defeat to Aston Villa Credit: talkSPORT

O'Hara appears to have lost all hope in Roberto De Zerbi's men after their 3-2 loss at home to Aston Villa on Saturday.

The result put Tottenham into the Premier League's bottom three and continued their nightmare winless start to the campaign.

As it stands, Spurs sit in 19th spot following Coventry's 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest, and they will sit bottom of the table heading into the international break if Fulham beat Manchester United on Sunday.



A third loss in five top-flight fixtures has seen Spurs fail to win any of their first five league games since the 2008/09 season.

And O'Hara launched into a defeated rant when speaking post-match alongside Cundy on talkSPORT's GameDay Phone-In.



Are Tottenham going down?

A baffled O'Hara said: "I can't believe how bad we are, genuinely, I can't believe how bad we are. Seriously, what has happened to this football club?

"What has happened to Spurs? [Sandro] Tonali, £100million, turning his back, Savio looks like he's playing kids' football, [Omar] Marmoush, who's he? Have we signed his brother? He is absolute guff.



"We haven't got a midfield, there's no fight in this team. None. No fight whatsoever, they're strolling about."

He then admitted: "We are so soft...it's the softest team in the Premier League, we're going to go down.

"I'm looking at the teams and it's like, everyone is better than us, right now, I'm looking at the bottom three and yeah, that is the bottom three right now, it looks like the bottom three.

3 Tottenham's misery continued as they failed to win again on Saturday afternoon Credit: Getty



"We've spent £400m to get away from the plughole and we're still in it! We're like that bit of food that gets stuck in the plug and you can't get rid of it...

"We're just in there, around the plughole and then eventually, you're going to go through it."

O'Hara attempts to walk out of studio

To make matters worse for O'Hara, he had to sit through the whole show with Cundy, who made sure to rub things in.

He stated: "In all honesty, you're going down. You will be doing EFL round-up next season..."



Typically, O'Hara would hit back at that, but on Saturday, he couldn't deny it, replying: "I feel like we actually will."

Cundy joked: "I think you need to start doing EFL round-up now, I'm serious now, we need to have an uncomfortable conversation."

3 Cundy blocked O'Hara from leaving as the ex-Spurs star got up to exit the studio Credit: talkSPORT

"I think we're in a relegation fight again, how is that acceptable? What is going on?" O'Hara then said.



Moments later, as Cundy's winding up continued and Spurs fan Rob called into the show with a more 'positive' outlook, O'Hara simply had enough and tried to leave the talkSPORT studio.

On Rob's suggestion to bring back Mauricio Pochettino and sign some players, he ranted: "It's literally the worst advice I have heard in my life, it's literally the worst ever, it's horrendous advice.

"Bring back Poch? Sign three good players and bring through four youth team players? What is this guff?"

He then got out of his chair and headed for the exit, but Cundy quickly blocked his path, saying: "No, no, no."



Unfortunately for O'Hara, that meant he had to stay in the room for the rest of the show and discuss Spurs a little longer...

Sports.title: Troy Deeney slams big-money Arsenal signing who ‘should have been hooked at half-time’
Sports.content:
Troy Deeney slams big-money Arsenal signing who ‘should have been hooked at half-time’

Mikel Arteta made a mistake in not hauling off Bruno Guimaraes at half-time in Arsenal’s 3-0 drubbing at Brighton.

That's the view of Troy Deeney, who was on on punditry duties for talkSPORT’s Game Day Live as the Gunners suffered their first defeat of the season at the Amex Stadium.



4 Bruno Guimaraes was singled out by Deeney as one of Arsenal's worst performers Credit: AFP

It was a day to forget for the Premier League champions who struggled to find their usual rhythm on the south coast, with Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andres all on target for the hosts.

Among the glut of underperforming stars, big money summer signing Guimaraes was singled out by Deeney.

What did Troy Deeney say about Bruno Guimaraes?

The Brazilian was unable to repeat his heroics from a week ago at Sunderland and the former Watford captain called for the £75million man to be hooked at the interval.



Arsenal boss Arteta did not immediately follow Deeney instructions, but the former Newcastle skipper was eventually replaced by Mikel Merino in the 59th minute.

Just minutes before the substitution, Deeney said: “There is no way Bruno Guimaraes can stay on this pitch; he's been really, really poor.”



Deeney also reserved criticism for Bukayo Saka who struggled to make the desired impact.

The winger was replaced by 16-year-old Max Dowman in the final ten minutes to cap off a frustrating afternoon.



Deeney followed up his assessment of Guimaraes by adding: “But I also think if we’re going to have that same level of pressure and expectation, Saka has been terrible.”

But the day belonged to a Brighton side who are now the Premier League’s top scorers with 16 goals from five matches – six more than any other team.

The win capped off a fine week for Fabian Hurzeler’s side who came in the match on the back of a 5-0 win at Coventry last weekend and a stunning comeback victory over Manchester United in midweek.

4 Brigton overpowered Arsenal at the Amex to take a deserved three points Credit: Getty



4 Mikel Arteta's side could find no answer to Brighton's high press Credit: Getty

Six of Brighton’s starters featured in Wednesday’s night’s 3-2 win at Old Trafford and provided a high-energy display of pressing and attacking prowess to keep the Gunners at bay.

The club’s supporters certainly enjoyed their final fixture before the international break and even found the time to issue a cheeky jibe at the Premier League champions.

After scoring their third, Brighton fans were heard chanting: “Are you Tottenham in disguise?” at the north London side.



The win moves Brighton provisionally up to third in the table, two points adrift of leaders Manchester City who host Sunderland on Sunday.

Hurzeler lauds his heroic stars

Following Saturday's 3-0 win, Hurzeler challenged his side to continue their momentum when the Premier League resumes in three weeks time.

"It's always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against," the Seagulls boss said.

4 Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler was all smiles after his side's superb display Credit: Getty



"Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels…we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league.

"My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

"Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level.

"We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going."

Sports.title: EFL club sack manager immediately after defeat with side sitting in relegation zone
Sports.content:
Peterborough United have sacked manager Luke Williams less than two hours after losing to Doncaster Rovers on Saturday.

Williams, who had been in charge of Posh since October last year, departs with the club sitting 23rd in League One.



2 Peterborough have sacked manager Williams immediately after losing to Doncaster Credit: Getty

The 2-0 defeat to Doncaster proved to be the final straw for the boss, with his side winning just one of their first seven games.

What did Peterborough say in their statement?

In a statement, Peterborough wrote: "Peterborough United Football Club has today parted company with First Team Manager Luke Williams.

"On behalf of everyone at the Football Club, we would like to place on record our thanks to Luke for all his efforts during his time at the Weston Homes Stadium.



"This is not a decision the club has taken lightly.

"However, the team's form in Sky Bet League One has not matched the Board's expectations, particularly given the significant investment made in the squad.

"And following today's performance against Doncaster Rovers, the Board felt it had no other choice but to make a change.



"The club's existing coaching staff will take charge of the first team squad while the Board considers its next steps."

Across his 11-month tenure at Posh, Williams took charge of 47 games and won 18, losing 20 and drawing eight.



Doncaster were bottom of League One heading into their clash at London Road on Saturday afternoon.

But their victory over Peterborough lifted them to 21st and dropped their opponents down to 23rd, leading to Williams' dismissal.

2 Williams took charge of 47 games for Posh, but departs after another loss Credit: Getty

A controversial ending

Williams leaves Peterborough just before reaching a year in charge.

But he departs amid controversy with the fans, having had to explain himself earlier this week following some post-match comments.



After beating Barnsley in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night, the Posh boss appeared to make a sarcastic remark towards supporters and their wishes.

Following a decision to switch to playing two strikers up front, he said: “If that’s what everyone wants, two strikers, then the middle of the pitch will be empty and it’s then impossible to control the game, but I’m here to try and give everyone what they want.”

He went on to clarify his comments on Thursday, but some fans were left surprised by his quotes.

And now, they have seen Williams sacked just seven games into the new League One campaign.

Sports.title: Jim Ratcliffe under fire as Manchester United fan group hit out over interview
Sports.content:
Jim Ratcliffe under fire as Manchester United fan group hit out over interview

Manchester United's Muslim Supporters' Club has issued a statement of no confidence in Jim Ratcliffe following his controversial comments.

The billionaire INEOS founder, who owns a large stake in the Red Devils, gave a controversial interview where he claimed the UK is 'on the slide' and named immigration as a contributing factor.



4 Ratcliffe acquired a 27.7 per cent stake in Man Utd in 2024 Credit: AFP

What did Jim Ratcliffe say?

Speaking on the BBC’s Big Boss Interview, Ratcliffe also claimed Britain once had 'the greatest empire in the world' before insisting this is no longer the case.

He said: “We had the greatest empire in the world, we were a great people. We won two world wars.

"We're good, honest folk, but unfortunately, at the moment, I think the UK is on the slide. It's quite difficult to see how we arrest it."



Ratcliffe added: “Nobody’s tough enough to deal with the immigration problem. Nobody’s tough enough to deal with the benefits problem.

“But somebody needs to do it.”

What has been said about Ratcliffe's comments?

In the wake of Ratcliffe's explosive comments, Man United's Muslim Supporters' Club have responded with a strong statement calling for Ratcliffe and other stakeholders - the Glazer family - to leave the club.



In a 750-word message, the fan group condemned Ratcliffe's remarks, as well as his decisions since acquiring a stake at the club in February 2024, having overseen rises in season ticket prices and controversial staff cost-cutting measures.

United's poor start to the season was also referenced, which hit a new low with their Carabao Cup collapse against Brighton this week.



The statement read: “Our players, staff, stewards, security teams and supporters come from different countries, cultures, ethnicities, religions and backgrounds.

“Manchester United would not be Manchester United without them. That diversity isn't a weakness of Manchester United. It is part of Manchester United.

4 Man United fans have previously voiced their frustrations with Ratcliffe's decisions since his arrival at Old Trafford in 2024 Credit: Getty

“Different backgrounds. Different beliefs. Different politics. One Manchester United.



“Manchester United does not belong emotionally to investment funds, shareholders or billionaires. It belongs to the generations of supporters who inherited this club from their parents and grandparents and who will one day pass it to their children.

“We love Manchester United. This club is all we know and, when it comes to football, it will be all we ever know. That is precisely why we cannot stay silent.

“This is bigger than one defeat. Bigger than one manager. Bigger than one season. It is about the direction, leadership and identity of Manchester United Football Club.

“After years of decline, broken promises and repeated failure, Manchester United Muslim Supporters' Club has lost confidence in the current ownership structure of Manchester United Football Club.



“Enough is enough. It is time for change. The Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe must go.”

4 Ratcliffe's two-year involvement at Man United has been far from straight forward Credit: Getty

This isn't the first time Ratcliffe has made controversial comments on immigration, who in February addressed his frustration at the government's approach and said the UK had been 'colonised by immigrants'.

In response, Man United put out a statement of their own highlighting the club's inclusive stance.



Ratcliffe went on to apologise if he 'offended some people', but his latest remarks have led the Red Devils' Muslim Supporters' Club to express their disappointment.

The statement continued: "Earlier this year, MUMSC publicly challenged Sir Jim Ratcliffe after his comments that the UK had been 'colonised by immigrants'.

"We condemned those comments then. He subsequently apologised for his choice of language,' the latest Muslim Supporters' Club statement read.

"We hoped a lesson had been learned. Clearly, it has not.

4 Ratcliffe's controversial comments come after Man United suffered back-to-back defeats to Manchester City and Brighton in recent days Credit: Getty



"This week, Sir Jim has again placed immigration and people receiving benefits at the centre of his explanation for Britain's problems, arguing that nobody is 'tough enough' to deal with either.

"We find these latest comments deeply disappointing and completely unacceptable."

Man United head into Sunday's clash with Fulham sitting 13th in the Premier League after gaining four points from their first four games.

Sports.title: Declan Rice avoids ‘clear red card’ for kicking out at Brighton player off the ball
Sports.content:
Declan Rice avoids ‘clear red card’ for kicking out at Brighton player off the ball

Declan Rice managed to avoid being sent off in the final seconds of Arsenal's 3-0 defeat to Brighton on Saturday afternoon.

The Gunners were dealt their first defeat of the Premier League season in shock fashion, with Rice losing his head late on.



3 Rice and Arsenal were battered by Brighton on Saturday, with the midfielder losing his cool late on Credit: Getty

In the last few moments of the clash at the Amex Stadium, with the Brighton fans bouncing, the midfielder kicked out.

Malick Yalcouye leaned into the England international, slightly nudging him, which caused a reaction.

Rice then chased down Yalcouye and swiped his legs from underneath him, sending him down to the ground.



As it happened, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook said on commentary: "Declan Rice goes through the back of Yalcouye off the ball! That looked a bit nasty!"

Co-commentator Troy Deeney then said: "Declan's just lost his temper there. There's no real need for it, there's a little push in the back.



"And as Yalcouye walks across him, he has a little swipe at his legs."

Crook went on to ask: "Is that not a red card?

To which Deeney replied: "You'd have to ask [Mikel] Arteta if he'd want that as a red card after his conference last week about referees."



Why was Rice not shown a red card?

Rice would only receive a yellow card for his actions - and the Premier League have now explained the decision not to send him off.

The incident was checked and cleared by VAR, but talkSPORT understands the VAR decided it did not meet the threshold for violent conduct, considering it to be petulant at best.

3 Rice managed to avoid a red card as VAR didn't deem his actions to be 'violent conduct' Credit: Getty

What has been said about Rice avoiding a red card?

Post-match, talkSPORT's Jason Cundy joined the debate over whether Rice should have been shown a red card.



He said: "My first instinct is that it should have been a red card."

With Deeney quickly agreeing: "It has to be a red card...Declan has lost his head for a brief second.

"If that was the other way around, they'd want someone sent off."

Speaking on the GameDay Phone-In, Cundy then stated: "It's a red card, he's a lucky boy, he should be off the field.

"He gets a yellow, it's a red card, VAR should get involved in that, he boots him off the ball, it's worse than the [Phil] Foden-Bruno [Fernandes] challenge last week, it's 100 per cent worse.

3 Arsenal's 3-0 defeat to Brighton was their heaviest on over three years Credit: Getty



"It's a red card, and this story won't go away, he's a lucky boy and it should have been a red card."

The 3-0 loss to Brighton was Arsenal's heaviest defeat in over three years and came as somewhat of a surprise, despite the clear quality of Fabian Hurzeler's Seagulls.

The Gunners had only conceded one goal this season up until this match, with their defence finally opened up.

As a result of the heavy defeat, they have now dropped down to second in the Premier League table behind Manchester City, who are yet to play this weekend and face Sunderland on Sunday.



Fortunately for Arteta though, he'll still have Rice available for their next clash after he managed to avoid a red.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi brands Tottenham the most fragile team he’s coached in 14 years
Sports.content:
"In my 14 years as a coach, I've never seen a team like us."

Roberto De Zerbi has been left in disbelief at how 'fragile' his Tottenham side is after their misery continued on Saturday.

3 De Zerbi watched on as his Spurs side were beaten yet again at home on Saturday Credit: AFP



Spurs were beaten 3-2 by Aston Villa to drop into the Premier League relegation zone on an embarrassing afternoon.

De Zerbi's side looked to be heading for a 3-0 loss, which would have seen them go five games without scoring a single goal after seeing Mohammed Kudus' tap-in ruled out by VAR.

But late strikes from Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke made the result look a lot more respectable on paper.

In reality though, it was another very rough day for Tottenham, who spent over £300million on transfers over the summer - and their manager seems as confused as their fans.



What has De Zerbi said about Tottenham's defeat to Aston Villa?

Speaking post-match, De Zerbi admitted that he is baffled by his own players following their third loss of the season.

"It's a mental aspect for sure, but they have the right mentality," the Italian told talkSPORT. "They work very well, they are good players.



"It's difficult to explain because, in my career, 14 years as a coach, I've never seen one team like us. So fragile, so inconsistent.

"You're good, or you're bad. You can't be very good in the first 30, 40 minutes, and then concede like this in this way.



"It's tough to accept for me."

De Zerbi has managed nine clubs in his 14 years on the touchline, but he is facing the toughest challenge of his career at Spurs.

3 Spurs' boss has been left in disbelief at how his side continue to disappoint Credit: Getty

What else did De Zerbi say?

The Tottenham manager was also asked if he could explain the 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

To which he admitted: "Listen, I'm a coach, but I do not have all the answers...for your question, I have no answer.



"I can say what I think, what I've seen today and I saw my team in the first half play very well, we had chances to score.

"We didn't score and then we conceded the first goal...we have to stay closer and stay stronger, more compact.

"In the second half, after Kudus' goal, I don't know if the players lost energy...now we have to explain another defeat."

De Zerbi added: "Maybe the communication between the players [is the problem], maybe the leaders have to be stronger.



3 De Zerbi has been unable to explain how his squad aren't able to put together a good performance Credit: Getty

"We need leaders to drive and lead the team...I don't know, I want to speak with the players when I stay with them.

"With Newcastle it was the same, in Liverpool it was the same, with Everton it was the same...we have to find the solutions."

Spurs have played 14 games in total under De Zerbi, winning on just four occasions and losing six in all competitions.



His points-per-game average in North London is 1.14, which is his lowest since 2018 when he was Benevento boss.

Across all of his matches at Tottenham, his side have conceded 19 goals and only managed to score 16.

This season, their two goals in the loss to Aston Villa are their only goals in the Premier League after five games, of which they have failed to win one - losing three and drawing two.

Sports.title: Man United's green shoots, Arsenal's goal struggles continue and Phallon Tullis-Joyce shines: THINGS WE LEARNED from the Gunners' late draw in blockbuster WSL clash
Sports.content:
Man United's green shoots, Arsenal's goal struggles continue and Phallon Tullis-Joyce shines: THINGS WE LEARNED from the Gunners' late draw in blockbuster WSL clash

Arsenal snatched a late draw at home against Manchester United to ensure their unbeaten start to the season remained intact.

Julia Zigiotti Olme gave United the lead midway through the second half, but Eva Olid’s side were unable to withstand a late onslaught from the hosts.

Smilla Holmberg finally found the back of the net in the fifth minute of stoppage time.

Daily Mail Sport’s women’s football reporter TARA ANSON-WALSH was at the Emirates to bring you the things we learned...

Arsenal's Holmberg finally found the back of the net in the fifth minute of stoppage time

Julia Zigiotti Olme gave struggling United the lead midway through the second half, but Eva Olid’s side were unable to withstand a late onslaught from the hosts

Green shoots at United

After the worst start to a WSL campaign in their history, both in terms of points (zero) and goals conceded (seven), following an opening-day defeat by London City Lionesses and a 5-0 thrashing at the hands of Chelsea, the last thing United needed was a trip to the Emirates.

It will have been a pleasant surprise to United fans, then, to have seen this resilient performance at one of the WSL’s toughest grounds. It also suggested that the tinkering behind the scenes by new manager Eva Olid may be beginning to take shape.

The Spanish manager has repeatedly called for her side to be braver, and they were that and then some here.

Where they spent their first couple of games in a hurry to implement Olid’s desire to attack, they were more patient here, and it paid off. Hinata Miyazawa and Julia Zigiotti Olme were superb in midfield, and Zigiotti Olme was rewarded with her poacher’s goal in the 67th minute.

Hinata Miyazawa and Julia Zigiotti Olme were superb in midfield, and Zigiotti Olme was rewarded with her poacher’s goal in the 67th minute

An undercooked pass back to Steph Catley from Georgia Stanway was seized upon by the Swedish midfielder, who coolly slotted home before speeding over to celebrate in front of the United fans. The exuberant celebrations from the whole squad pointed to a clear moment of catharsis after a torrid start to the season.

Olid, who is clear in where she wants to take the team, said after the match: 'It's been an intense week, because there were a lot of emotions from the players, from the staff. No one wants to lose 5-0 (to Chelsea).

'I think this week we grew as a team. The first day after we lost 5-0, it was not easy for anyone. And then we spoke and we said "listen, we need energy, that is the most important thing this week. We need a positive mindset and to work hard".

'The focus was on the defensive shape and in attack to have more confidence. (Against Arsenal) we had more possession in the first half in periods, we were having the ball, but it's about being more creative. Keeping the fine, but now we need to break the last line of pressure and create more chances to score more goals.'

Arsenal profligate in front of goal

As this game dragged into the closing minutes, another missed chance by Arsenal was met by a chorus of groans.

Time and time again, the Gunners were unable to find the back of the net. Olivia Smith, usually one to rely on for a worldie, spent much of the game frustrated by her marker, Anna Sandberg.

Alessia Russo also struggled to provide any impact, while Stina Blackstenius was denied from a strong position by Phallon Tullis-Joyce at the end of the first half. Mariona Caldentey was unable to keep a curling shot down and Leah Williamson was unable to find enough power with a shot of her own also in the opening 45 minutes.

Russo struggled to impact the game and was kept quiet by a resilient United defensive display

Heading into this game, Arsenal had scored just once from 43 shots in their opening two games, and they appeared to be heading for their first back-to-back league games without a goal in three years until Holmberg rectified the damage in the last minute of the match.

Renee Slegers is clear that this is an area that her team need to address. Her assessment of her team's performance was met by a simple: 'Not turning dominance into danger.'

She later added: 'If I look at the last two games and dominance and not converting that into goals and wins, that's something we have to look at.

'We believe in the quality of the squad, the quality of ideas of the players, and the things that we can create in a variety of ways. When that starts clicking, it's going to be really good, so it really is about the details in the final third.'

Phallon Tullis-Joyce worth her weight in gold

Manchester United goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce put in another superb display on Saturday.

While she may be limited in her long-range distribution, she more than makes up for it with her shot-stopping abilities.

Her best moment came deep into the first half, when Stina Blackstenius’ header was hit with power and appeared destined for the roof of the net, only for the 29-year-old to tip it over.

In the second half, Tullis-Joyce popped up again, keeping out Caitlin Foord’s low shot from reaching the far-right corner of her goal.

The American shot-stopper is still being considered by Emma Hayes among a pool of candidates to wear the No 1 jersey for the record four-time world champions at next summer’s Brazil World Cup.

How United fare this season could impact those chances. More performances like this, though, from both her and her team, and she’ll be on that plane.

Manchester United goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce put in another superb display here at the Emirates on Saturday

What you give is what you get

There’s nowhere quite like the Emirates for putting into perspective the difference in meaningful investment between two WSL sides.

The Lionesses’ European successes have been watershed moments in the evolution of the women’s game, and savvy clubs such as Arsenal have capitalised. At the Emirates on Saturday, there were 29,853 in attendance. This is the norm these days.

Recent research conducted ahead of the new season shows that the boom in popularity of women’s football is not going to slow down any time soon.

Data collected by Nielsen, a leading firm in media measurement, analytics and insights, showed that the average standalone valuation of women’s football sponsorship deals has increased by 42 per cent over the past year alone.

There’s nowhere quite like the Emirates for putting into perspective the difference in meaningful investment between two WSL sides

The WSL has emerged as a standard-bearer for this commercial progress. Barclays has doubled its previous financial commitment as title partner, taking the investment to £30million over three years.

There have also been bridges into popular culture, illustrated by the women’s football focus of the latest series of Ted Lasso and Nike’s recent record-breaking deal with London City Lionesses.

Manchester City Women launched their own women’s football brand a couple of weeks ago, while Brighton are building the first purpose-built women’s football stadium. Arsenal and Chelsea have relocated permanently to their men’s stadiums.

And Manchester United... well, what you see is what you get.

A decent squad of players, albeit one that was unnecessarily pared back in the summer. A very decent fanbase. A new, relatively inexperienced manager still learning the ropes.

And beyond that? Pretty much nada.

There is no talk of scaling up. No plans to relocate away from the 12,000-capacity Leigh Sports Village.

Imagine what would happen if Manchester United, the third most valuable club in the world according to Forbes, threw their hat into the WSL ring for real.

A trip to north London on a women's matchday weekend could give Jim Ratcliffe and Co a pretty good idea.

Sports.title: Coventry's Premier League campaign FINALLY has lift-off in controversial 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest: Relief for Frank Lampard as late equaliser is ruled out after VAR check
Sports.content:
A first Premier League win in over 25 years, off the foot of the table and finally some hope that Coventry can defy the odds and beat the drop.

Little wonder Frank Lampard celebrated wildly in front of 3,000 jubilant Sky Blues supporters at the final whistle.

A stunning 55th-minute strike from left wing-back Jay Dasilva left his boss a picture of delight and Forest still without a win at home this season.

After Coventry ended a run of four straight losses without scoring, Lampard smiled: 'We were really good – we played with personality and confidence.

'It was about work ethic and fight and then you have to get your goal and really dig in. We did that and I hope this can be a springboard.'

While Dasilva provided the coup de grace, this much-needed and deserved victory was all about the collective.

Frank Lampard led Coventry to their first Premier League win of the season over Nottingham Forest on Saturday

Jay Dasilva (second left) scored a fine winner and Coventry certainly made the most of the win

A brilliant clearance from visiting defender Bobby Thomas – who hacked Forest substitute Igor Jesus' goalbound shot off the line in the final quarter – said much for Coventry's refusal to buckle.

They needed good fortune in the closing stages, though, as Jesus fired home before a VAR check by referee Jarred Gillett ruled the striker had fouled Caleb Yirenkyi before shooting.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS NOTTM FOREST (3-4-2-1): Sels 6.5; Cunha 6, Diomande 6 (Wood 73, 6), Murillo 6; Munoz 6 (Netz 83), Schlager 6, McAtee 5.5 (Sangare 83), Williams 6; Ndoye 5.5 (Jesus 59, 6), Gibbs-White 6.5; Delap 5.5. Booked: Delap, Cunha. Manager: Oliver Glasner 5.5. COVENTRY (3-4-2-1): Rushworth 6.5; Mfuni 6.5, Thomas 7.5, Pinnock 6.5; Yirenkyi 6,5 (Latibeaudiere 90 +1), Onyeka 6, Grimes 6.5, DASILVA 8; Rudoni 6.5 (Simms 74, 6), Mason-Clark 6.5 (Tchaouna 46, 6); Thomas-Asante 6.5 Scorers: Dasilva 55. Manager: Frank Lampard 7.5. Referee: Jarred Gillet 6. Attendance: 30,666.

Lampard added: 'We bemoan VAR, but they got that one right.'

Much has been made of Coventry's awful start to their first top-flight campaign since 2000-01, but scrutiny turned on Forest after this impotent display.

Boss Oliver Glasner said of the latest VAR controversy to afflict his team: 'Of course I have my thoughts but I don't want to speak about it again.'

Ex-England midfielder Lampard, one of the greatest players of his generation, constantly paced his technical area.

The 48-year-old's energy burst through his body for the entire game, seeping through his pores when Dasilva latched onto Carl Rushworth's long punt and coolly slotted home left-footed.

Lampard added: 'It was a great goal and really gave us something to hold on to.'

Not since a John Hartson header saw off Sunderland in April 2001 had Coventry fans seen their team win a game of Premier League football.

They have now. And how they celebrated.

Sports.title: West Ham star Taty Castellanos being accused of SPITTING at Millwall goalkeeper a rare flashpoint as meeting of football's fiercest rivalries ends without major incident despite 14-year wait, writes JAMES SHARPE
Sports.content:
They had waited 14 years for this. For the latest edition of what’s been christened the Dockers’ Derby, the meeting of two of football’s fiercest rivals, these two old firms, ones depicted in the films Green Street and Football Factories. Julian Dicks, the former West Ham defender, got hit with a brick once.

But for as ready as these supporters may have been, the police were even more so. The Met deployed more than 400 officers, four times the size of the usual football task force, some with dogs, others on horses, many armed with riot gear. They had facial recognition at their disposal and set up a dispersal zone spreading nearly five miles south of the river while the City of London Police put in their own north of the Thames.

As West Ham fans strolled down 'Cowards’ Way', the enclosed path taken by away fans from South Bermondsey station towards to the Den, it was not Millwall supporters who greeted them from below the bridge underneath as they passed but lines of riot vans and police officers with their German Shepherds. No one was getting through there.

And as much as you could feel the bubbling tension - and, boy, could you feel the tension - it still rarely felt primed to burst.

West Ham’s team bus received an expectedly hostile greeting as it pulled up to the Den, as home fans lined up to pass on their best wishes but, even then, nothing was pelted towards it. No drinks, let alone bricks.

One officer outside South Bermondsey station clocked a West Ham fan sipping from his canned M&S gin and tonic. How times have changed.

Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall appeared to allege that West Ham forward Taty Castellanos spat at him

Marschall made the accusation during a feisty Dockers Derby between Millwall and West Ham

West Ham deny their striker Taty Castellanos spat at the goalkeeper on Saturday



But this is The Den, of course, and a day like this was never going to go by without something threatening to unravel it all. As the home fans were funnelled out of the ground to the surrounding streets after this frenetic 2-2 draw which saw West Ham come from two goals down to snatch a point, a small group began to clash with police on horseback.

One man was seized by two police offers and flung to the ground.

While it was all happening, other fans angrily shouted at journalists, Daily Mail Sport included, to stop filming and to ‘put your f***ing phones away’, and accused them of being ‘grasses’. One photographer was then threatened after telling one furious supporter that he was only doing his job.

The uprising, though, was extinguished as quickly as it had ignited. The vast number of police just had it under control.

By 4pm, the Met confirmed they had made just six arrests and those for incidents including tailgating, assaulting a police officer and trying to get into the Den while intoxicated. They nicked nearly twice as many Millwall fans outside a Hammers pub in Stratford the night before.

The biggest flashpoint, in the end, happened on the pitch when West Ham striker Taty Castellanos was accused of spitting at Filip Marschall as the Millwall goalkeeper refused to release the ball while the hosts were 2-0 up just after the hour.

‘I believe so,’ said Lions boss Alex Neil. ‘Fil was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened. Fil would say that without cause. I’m sure the referees and the authorities will look at it and if it warrants that it needs dealt with, I’m sure they will.’

Daily Mail Sport are not welcome at the Den, with the publication still banned from attending matches, so we found our vantage point on one of the paths that run alongside the train track next to the stadium where lads stood on Lime Bikes to peer over a metal fence and between the gap in the corner between two stands.

You could hear the febrile roars and see the flying limbs as Caleb Taylor gave Millwall the lead, finally bundling the ball into the net despite the heroic attempts of West Ham goalkeeper, which got louder still when Camiel Neghli bundled in from a long throw to make it two before the break.

If anyone was here for a fight, it didn’t appear to be West Ham. And yet, with about a quarter of an hour to go, substitute Mo Kante fired a low shot into the corner to pull one back before Konstantinos Mavropanos headed in the equaliser five minutes later.

Kyrell Lisbie raced clear in the closing minutes for Millwall only for Kante to haul him down before he could slot home the winner to earn himself a red card and a place in Hammers fans’ hearts.

And so, after waiting for so long, none of them had the bragging rights. The big winners, by a distance, were the Met.

Sports.title: Injury-hit Newcastle show their mettle to hold the Hull onslaught at bay as brave performance helps banish ghosts of Leeds drubbing, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
It was starting to feel very England v Argentina for Newcastle and their German manager, but this time the team in retreat held on. Hull did not have Lionel Messi, of course.

At 2-0 up with half an hour to play, the hosts hit reverse. They conceded ground and possession and a barrage of shots. There were 21 in total come the end. Their head coach, Matthias Jaissle, could do little to change the direction in which his players were headed.

And so, during a close that felt as much like attack v defence on a training ground, Newcastle kicked, blocked and hoped, and all of it from the discomfort of their own penalty area.

They deserve some credit for that. When Mohamed-Ali Cho slotted a reply for Hull in the 67th minute, an equaliser felt inevitable. More so, you suspected the visitors would even go on to land a knockout blow.

But home captain Malick Thiaw gloved up and it was he who led the resistance. The centre-back and his team-mates were fortunate to emerge with three points, but amid an injury crisis and ahead of a 23-day break before they next play, there is no under-estimating the magnitude of this victory for Newcastle.

‘I’m overall really proud,’ said Jaissle. ‘We needed to suffer. We defended with heart and commitment and that was exceptional.'

Lewis Hall put Newcastle 2-0 up after 25 minutes against Hull - but the hosts didn't have it all their own way

Matthias Jaissle's side showed their mettle to hold onto a vital victory at St James' Park

On the back of Monday’s 4-1 drubbing at Leeds and fierce criticism for a performance and result many felt was due despite an unbeaten start, Jaissle had demanded a response. He got one – and it was fast, direct and immediate. If Hull were expecting to meet a Newcastle side low on confidence, they found one high on energy. Not just that, they had ideas, too.

Harvey Barnes was the architect behind most of them and, come the seventh minute, Newcastle had two goals and he had two assists. The first was a clever reverse pass that presented Joe Willock with an opening to fire on goal, and that he duly did, lashing into the bottom corner from ten yards.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 6; Miley 6, Thiaw 8, Botman 7, Hall 7; Steur 8 (Schar 66, 6), Willock 7 (Bamba 87); Murphy 6, Wissa 6, Barnes 7; Fernandez-Pardo 5 (Toure 74, 6) Subs not used: Pope, Thompson, Pivas, Salia, M Miley, Mills. Manager: Matthias Jaissle 6 HULL (5-4-1): Tzolakis 7; Coyle 6, Ajayi 6, Egan 6 (Vaz 78, 6), Herrington 6, Giles 7; Belloumi 7 (Gelhardt 83), Crooks 5 (Iroegbunam 46, 6), Slater 6 (Gourna-Douath 78, 5), Thomas 5 (Cho 63, 7); McBurnie 7 Subs not used: Phillips, Hjerto-Dahl, McNair, Stroud. Manager: Sergej Jakirović 6 Ref: T Harrington 7

Lewis Hall’s low finish four minutes later was from a little further out and found the opposite corner, but that goal also owed as much to the endeavour of Barnes. The winger drove through the middle of the pitch and beyond three blue jerseys before slipping left to the scorer just inside the area.

What had threatened to be a nervy stadium, with a fragile home team within it, was suddenly a place of calm reassurance. Sean Steur, still just 18 years old, was running the game from midfield. Willock, alongside him, was doing the more literal running.

Newcastle were in control, and then they weren’t. The drift was just setting in when, on the stroke of half-time, they won a penalty and the chance to kill the game. It looked a soft award, the hand of Sorba Thomas clipping the heel of Jacob Murphy, causing him to stumble.

But it was a gift they could not take. Yoane Wissa’s spot-kick was well placed but lacked the power to beat the dive of Konstantinos Tzolakis and the goalkeeper saved brilliantly.

‘The start was a high level and the right response,’ said Jaissle. ‘We should have killed the game. We totally dominated the first half. The missed penalty gave them hope. We then had tired bodies on the pitch.’

The second half belonged to Hull. Mohamed Belloumi twice slammed over from good positions before Newcastle lost Steur to fatigue in the 66th minute. Within 60 seconds, Belloumi robbed Lewis Miley and set Cho away to score.

From that point on, the home goalmouth became this city’s most densely populated space. It was chaos. For Newcastle, there was certainly no control. Unlike England, however, they survived – even if only just.

Sports.title: More VAR controversy hits the Premier League, how Thierno Barry is still a work in progress after scoring winner for Everton and why Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil deserves credit despite defeat
Sports.content:
More VAR controversy hits the Premier League, how Thierno Barry is still a work in progress after scoring winner for Everton and why Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil deserves credit despite defeat

Can we go just one week in the Premier League without VAR taking centre stage?

Here, on the banks of the River Mersey, with Everton rocking and rolling, Thierno Barry produced a brilliant header from near post to far post to make it 2-0 from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's corner.

The South Stand erupted, just as it had when Ainsley Maitland-Niles salvaged a point against Manchester United last time out here. Barry brought out the dance moves. Then came the dreaded big screen announcement of a VAR check.

Brennan Johnson was stood in front of Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton, drafted into the side with No 1 Kjell Scherpen dropped, and that was enough for VAR Andrew Kitchen and referee Stuart Atwell to rule it out.

Johnson was stood in an offside position, that much was correct. But to defiantly say he was interfering with Walton's ability to make the save is not. Walton had hedged to his left as the ball flew into the other corner, way out of his reach, regardless of the Welshman stood on his toes.

'The word used was affected his ability to save it which I don't think was the case,' David Moyes said.

Everton were relieved to see out a win against Ipswich Town which VAR almost ruined

Thierno Barry's near post header was flicked impressively in at the far post to make it 2-0

Brennan Johnson (left) was stood offside but was adjudged to be impeding the goalkeeper

'It is difficult for referees. Do I think we will get consistency through the season? I doubt it. The goalkeeper would not have saved the header.'

It is hard to escape the feeling that last week's mishandling of the Manchester derby in which Enzo Fernandez was clearly interfering moments before Erling Haaland converted the match-winning goal had played a role in the rush to chalk this one off.

'Everton No.22 is in an offside position,' Atwell announced in the stadium. 'He impacts the goalkeeper's ability to save the ball. My final decision is indirect free-kick.'

Even at the final whistle, with Barry's fortuitous first-half goal, which saw him deflect James Tarkowski's long-range strike in off his chest, the difference between the sides, the boos for Atwell and his assistants was as loud as anything else.

'I don't understand why the [second] goal was offside because the goalkeeper can do nothing [to prevent] the goal,' Barry said afterwards.

Everton are up to fifth, still unbeaten, dreaming of Europe, but still find themselves asking: why is VAR in such a rush to chalk off goals?

BARRY STILL A WORK IN PROGRESS

Barry finished with one, was denied what looked a legitimate second, and in the eyes of his manager, really should have walked away with a hat-trick after spurning a glorious header in the first half which had him sunk to his knees when it whistled past the post.

Barry is a fascinating player to watch. So many of the fundamentals are there. He works hard. Always finds himself in scoring positions. He is also one of only two Premier League players to score five or more goals in all competitions this season alongside Erling Haaland (six). Not bad company to keep.

But those inside the dressing room feel like they haven't even scratched the surface when it comes to the 23-year-old.

'Coming in to the Premier League for the first time as a striker isn't easy,' Moyes said.

Barry is a fascinating project to study - and those inside Everton believe lots more is to come

'We took a bit of a risk at the time, a young striker and we thought 'here we go, we'll have a go with it'.

'He's got an awful lot of good attributes. But we want him to score! My goodness, with the opportunities you could have scored, should have scored his header today which would have made it 2-0.

'He works really hard, he tries, he's still settling in but he's doing a good job.'

It's hard to root against Barry. His smile lights up a stadium and while he can look so raw in moments and so finessed in others, it's easy to see why team-mates are quick to jump to his defence at the first sign of criticism.

'He works hard and the goals will come from working hard,' Jordan Pickford said of his striker.

'The first year in the Premier League is always tough, he has found his feet and he has started a lot better this year.'

Golden boot? Steady on. But lots more is to come from Barry, that's for sure.

BRAVE O'NEIL WILL BE REWARDED

It is testament to the culture Gary O'Neil is trying to build as Ipswich Town boss that even when down to 10 men – Abdul Fatawu has a lot of apologies to make to his team-mates and manager after picking up a second yellow card for diving – he went full throttle to score.

On came strikers Chuba Akpom and Zian Flemming and there Ipswich pushed, now in a 4-3-2 shape, willing to risk conceding that sucker-punch second goal.

O'Neil was brave, too, to drop his No 1 goalkeeper, a summer recruit from Belgium that arrived to great acclaim. He had had chances and hadn't taken them. 'Form' Next man up.

This was by no means a disaster for Ipswich, who managed to create genuine anxiety in the ranks of Everton fans, and they head back to Suffolk with plenty to ponder.

They have technicians in the middle of the park, attacking full-backs and enough artillery in attacking areas to cause plenty of teams problems.

But pretty football, as they showed on numerous occasions here, only counts for so much if you aren't going to put the ball in the back of the net.

MATCH FACTS AND RATINGS Everton (4-2-3-1): Pickford 6; Maitland-Niles 7 (O’Brien 90+1), Tarkowski 6, Branthwaite 7, Mykolenko 6; Garner 6, Armstrong 5; Johnson 6 (Dibling 66, 8), Dewsbury-Hall 6 (Hackney 90+1), Grealish 6 (George 79, 6); Barry 7 Goals: Barry (11) Booked: Mykolenko, Armstrong Manager: David Moyes 7 Ipswich Town (4-2-3-1): Walton 6; Ouattara 7, Diop 6, O’Shea 6, Davis 7; Lukic 5 (Florentino 73, 7), Palacios 6 (Akpom 81, 6); Fatawu 3, Enciso 7 (Maeda 74, 5), Clarke 6 (Philogene 66, 5); Emersonn 5 (Flemming 81, 6) Booked: Fatawu, Flemming Red card: Fatawu Manager: Gary O’Neil 6 Referee: Stuart Atwell 4 Att: 52,008

Gary O'Neil was bold, even when down to 10 men, and that will pay off in the longer term

'We have to punish teams like they punish us when they get the opportunity,' defender Leif Davis said.

'When we went to 10 men I think we were the better team. We're a hard team to play against and, while we were beaten, there are a lot of positives to take.'

His manager was also of the mind that his team deserved more than they got.

'I thought we had a good go today and the result is harsh on the lads,' O'Neil said.

'We restricted Everton to not very much. Really unlucky with the goal, played some good stuff but lacked quality when we got in front of goal.

'If we keep playing like that, we will give teams a game every week and we just need to keep repeating that.'

Sports.title: England surge to No 1 in T20 rankings with another dominant win over hapless Sri Lanka as Jos Buttler stars
Sports.content:
England's outrageous Twenty20 form saw them obliterate Sri Lanka in Manchester, propelling them back to the top of the world rankings in the process.

Jos Buttler finished the contest by swatting a one-handed six over midwicket, symbolising the ease with which Harry Brook's team chased down their 125-run target. They required just 58 of their allotted 120 deliveries.

And so with a 20th win in 22 they displaced India in first place, having briefly dislodged the world champions by beating them 4-0 earlier this summer.

Neatly, this particular sequence of results began on this ground 12 months ago when England piled up 304 for two against South Africa, the record total between two Test playing nations.

'You never want to take the opportunity of whitewashing a side for granted and that's why we went with our strongest side. We obviously knew we had the chance to go No 1 in this series if we beat them 3-0, so that was always in the back of our minds,' beamed Brook.

'Now, we have got to stay motivated, to try to keep that spot for as long as possible. We don't play as much T20 as other nations, especially India, so keeping that might not be as easy as it sounds, but every opportunity we get, we are going to try to dominate the opposition.'

Jos Buttler starred for England as they romped to another dominant T20 win over Sri Lanka

The team continue to impress under Harry Brook (centre) and are now ranked No 1 in the world

Sri Lanka have not defeated England in this format for 12 years and that statistic was not remotely challenged, as they slumped from 107 for four to 124 all out, with the farcical penultimate dismissal of Wanindu Hasaranga – who dislodged the leg bail with a flourish of his bat after missing a delivery from Jofra Archer.

Two wickets for Sonny Baker, taking his series figures to six for 44 – at a miserly economy rate of 3.71 – set the tone. Jamie Overton kept up the pressure through the middle overs, sending down 14 dot balls in taking one for 15.

And the ruthless nature of this England team was highlighted by Buttler's finale: in smiting Eshan Malinga for 18 off four balls, including his only two sixes of the innings, he finished unbeaten on 62 off 32.

Sri Lanka crumbled under the pressure, allowing Brook to get off the mark via a misfield. He departed to a run out, after adding 33 from 21. It felt like the only way Sri Lanka would dismiss him such was the disdain with which he treated their bowlers.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta fumes at Arsenal stars after 3-0 thumping by Brighton: Gunners boss warns defeat was a 'big lesson' as Bruno Guimaraes reveals angry response in dressing room after 'unacceptable' display
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta fumes at Arsenal stars after 3-0 thumping by Brighton: Gunners boss warns defeat was a 'big lesson' as Bruno Guimaraes reveals angry response in dressing room after 'unacceptable' display

An upset Mikel Arteta branded Brighton's pummelling of Arsenal as a 'big lesson' which had left him 'extremely disappointed' with his players on a shock afternoon for the reigning Premier League champions.

Goals from Pascal Gross and Charalampos Koustoulas put the Seagulls ahead by half-time, before Chema Andres' header added the gloss on an emphatic display.

The Gunners had been dominated from the start, leaving Arteta furious over his team's performance. It ends their seven-game unbeaten run across all competitions, and is Arsenal's first league defeat since last April against Manchester City.

Arteta said: 'Extremely disappointed, but first of all, I think we have to congratulate Brighton for the victory. I think they deserve it, they were the better team.

'Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and not respecting the game.

'And from our side there were certain basics that you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from.

Mikel Arteta said he was 'extremely disappointed' after Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton

Arteta admitted he had a negative feeling early on in the game in an abject display from his side

'In the first duel, the second ball, that put the game, especially how direct they were, in a really difficult place for us.

'On top of that, when we did regain the ball, especially in our own half, the amount of technical errors that we did and we didn't respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations.

'That put us always on the back foot, so it was very difficult to control the game. When we had moments of dominance and control, we opened them up, but we didn't finish those actions with the quality that is required.

'So at the end of the day, I think they deserve to win the game and it's a big lesson for us.'

Bruno Guimaraes was also left angry about the display and said players were complaining about it in the changing room.

'I think today is a day to forget,' said Guimaraes. 'Everything we tried didn't work. Credit to them (Brighton) as well but we can't accept this here.

'I think in the changing room, everyone was complaining about ourselves, about the level we played today. Like I said, it's not acceptable. A very bad day in the office.'

Arteta admitted he had a negative feeling about the upcoming result from the very start of the game.

'From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear,' he said.

'We put ourselves in trouble one time, two times, three times and we need to get out of that much quicker than that. That's one of the biggest lessons that we have to take from the game today.'

Meanwhile, an elated Hurzeler was full of praise for his Brighton team.

He said: 'It was a special win. Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It's always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against.'

Asked if it was the best result of his career, Hurzeler added: 'It is a difficult question to ask immediately after the game when the emotions are still high.

'It is very important to stay humble. We have to enjoy this moment, but understand why we had success, and come back to our roots which is about being brilliant in the basics,and trusting each other.'

Sports.title: Timid Arsenal were BULLIED by Brighton in 3-0 defeat: This performance from Mikel Arteta's men beggared belief and proves it is far too early to write off title challengers yet, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Timid Arsenal were BULLIED by Brighton in 3-0 defeat: This performance from Mikel Arteta's men beggared belief and proves it is far too early to write off title challengers yet, writes ISAAN KHAN

Timid and shellshocked. Bullied. Rarely have such words been attributed to Arsenal in recent times.

Even those with a liking to Mikel Arteta’s team would struggle to utter more positive terms. By full-time, the Seagulls had pecked holes through each Arsenal player, and Arteta’s tactical sheets, on the club’s 125th anniversary. What an emphatic way to mark it.

Even the home fans had chants of ‘are you Tottenham in disguise?’ and ‘champions of England, you’re having a laugh’ in full flow, not afraid of revving up a wounded Arsenal team completely off the boil.

The score ended 3-0. Though, on another afternoon, four or five nil would have been more fitting. Even the typically composed Declan Rice decided to boot Malick Yalcouye in frustration seconds before the full-time whistle, somehow escaping a red card.

This was a Gunners display synonymous of their side from four or five years ago, when the Spaniard had started paving the building blocks towards a Premier League title competing side.

What transpired here on the south coast defied belief. All teams can have an off day. No side is truly unbeatable in this league, even if the hype around Arsenal had reached silly levels because of the sheer frailties of the other Big Six members.

Yet, the manner in which Fabian Hurzeler’s relentless Brighton had run straight through the visitors sent a warning to the league. This season’s champions is not a forgone conclusion. Far from it.

Mikel Arteta's Arsenal side were bullied by Brighton as they lost 3-0 on Saturday afternoon

Right from the start, Arsenal were completely at sea. David Raya’s passes were laced with panic, many reaching his team-mates with too much power; a few even breached the touchline. That is a rare sight indeed.

The backline looked nervy. The midfield were being cut through at will, Bruno Guimaraes, on his first start for the club, not syncing with Rice; the tenacity of Myles Lewis-Skelly, on the bench, was arguably missed. The frontline were hidden.

Pascal Gross, one of Brighton’s many in-form players, had struck on 31 minutes to set the rout off. He received the ball outside the area, Arsenal’s backline dropping off, as if to say, ‘Go on, try, your luck’.

He did just that, lashing the ball with pace towards goal, rebounding off the bottom-right post and into the net. Riccardo Calafiori was the main culprit. He should’ve stepped forward to challenge. Still, it was an excellent strike befitting a man in red hot form. Gross now has seven goals contributions across all competitions this season.

Diego Gomez’s assist before half-time followed a similar pattern, the backline backing off. He passed to Charalampos Kostoulas, who swivelled outside the area and struck past Raya from 25 yards out.

Another goal was to follow, courtesy of Chema Andres from a Gross corner kick. Yet by the end, the Brighton players were queuing for their turn to strike at goal like kids at a half-time football challenge.

Substitute Matt O’Riley had his one-on-one shot save by Raya on 89 minutes which Yalcouye latched on to hit the crossbar, for example.

Brighton deserve enormous credit, a side which outfought, outthought and outran Arsenal. Not many sides in recent times can claim as such. They are so well-drilled and have struck 16 goals in the league, compared to the visitors’ eight. That is a marked difference.

Having warded off a clawing by the Black Cats, Arsenal had a pecking by the seagulls to overcome.

The animosity around Hurzeler’s comments last season, where he criticised Arsenal’s style of play, may have been forgiven by Arteta though the German was in no mood for a friendly-natured fixture.

It could have been more than three, too, with the champions suffering their first loss of the season

The Premier League’s best attack vs best defence, thus far, was the billing. Brighton started fiercely on the front foot. Diego Gomes stayed on Calafiori like a hare, refusing to give him an inch.

Each time the ball arrived on his flank within the first 10 minutes, Gomes was on the Italian’s foot.

The home side had registered three attempts — one on target — within the first 10 minutes, illustrating how front-footed they had set up.

In truth, Raya’s pass out of play on two minutes had set the tone for an afternoon only going in one direction.

It took until 18 minutes for Arsenal’s attempt first at goal, Guimaraes’ cross-shot whacking the side netting.

When Gross struck, an inevitability had been felt. There was a general sloppiness across the pitch, the Arsenal midfield struggling to string passes together.

They nearly grabbed a goal back on the cusp of half-time, Martin Odegaard marching forward on a counter-attack.

His shot, saved by Bart Verbruggen, rebounded into the path of Bukayo Saka who could only scuff his attempt.

Pascal Gross, one of Brighton's many in-form players, struck early on to set the tone

The winger hit the turf face down, in dismay at his prolificacy. By the team he had looked up, Brighton were in the opposite half.

Gomez latched on to a pass and drove forward, supplying Kostoulas. He swivelled outside the area and struck past Raya.

Whatever transpired in the Arsenal dressing room at half-time, it clearly didn’t work. It will have been some scene, nevertheless, Arteta expectedly incensed at what he had watched from a team stamping their authority on the league — not just chasing three points.

A win here would have been an eighth consecutive win across all competitions, equalling the club’s 123-year record for their best start to a campaign.

That quickly became clearly unattainable. Raya’s first action of the second period was to hoof the ball out of play, an early sign that Arsenal were not going to improve anytime soon.

Ferdi Kadioglu fell to the deck under pressure from Calafiori, referee Darren England waving away the penalty call.

Nothing went Arsenal's way - they now have an international break to mull over their struggles

Later, Gross’ corner found the head of Andres to put Brighton three goals ahead, the midfielder rising above Gabriel and Calafiori to head home.

Kai Havertz found himself one-on-one with Verbruggen on 78 minutes, Viktor Gyokeres’ clever chipped pass finding the striker.

He should have scored — but the ball rebounded off Verbruggen’s leg.

It summed Arsenal up on a day where nothing went their way — and a bright red warning sign travelled to all their rivals across the league.

Sports.title: 'It stinks' - Steven Gerrard fires JJ Gabriel warning as clubs circle for Man Utd youngster
Sports.content:
'It stinks' - Steven Gerrard fires JJ Gabriel warning as clubs circle for Man Utd youngster

JJ Gabriel has informed Manchester United he wants to leave the club, but Steven Gerrard has issued a stark warning to the youngster

View 2 Images Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel reportedly wants to leave Old Trafford. (Image: (Photo by Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has warned JJ Gabriel that he'll face identical challenges at Manchester United and Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho, amid an ongoing tussle over the wonderkid and providing a route into the first-team.

‌



The 15-year-old informed United of his desire to leave amid speculation linking him with La Liga heavyweights Real and Barcelona, having been poised for his United debut in midweek.

‌



The teenager delivered the shock news that he wanted his registration cancelled at Old Trafford, and has not turned out for any of the Reds' sides since. United manager Michael Carrick urged restraint concerning Gabriel following the loss to Brighton.

‌



Carrick said: "It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really. He's certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we have to be careful about the exposure on that one."

Man Utd Muslim supporters group demand Jim Ratcliffe exit after statement on UK decline READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

That view has now been shared by Gerrard, who insists Gabriel's career requires safeguarding. Speaking to TNT Sports, Gerrard said: "It's not just in this situation. Broadly, it scares me in the game that kids can now be rushed or careers can be forced.

‌



"I don't know the details and the background in this isolated situation with JJ Gabriel, but if you look at it all, he's at one of the biggest clubs in the world. They've got a history and a tradition of producing fantastic players.

"There will be top people behind the scenes at Manchester United but the big thing for me is, you've got an English coach [Michael Carrick] and an English assistant manager [Steve Holland] who will want to, when the time is right, and when they think he's ready, protect him... but when they feel he's ready they will play him.

"Not just this situation, the game as a whole, these talents, they have parents, they have agents, outside influences that force and rush too soon, and it can affect a kid's career.

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel won't be playing for England in the upcoming international break (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

"It is going to add huge pressure, and also if you're another club looking into this situation, you're thinking to yourself, 'yeah, the kid is a big talent', but do you want the baggage and the noise around it?

"Let's use Jose Mourinho for example at Real Madrid. Even if he goes to Real Madrid now, is Jose Mourinho going to play this kid straight away? Is he going to be forced to push him? You know what these elite managers are like, they play kids when they are ready to contribute to the team.

Article continues below

"In my opinion they need to look after the kid's health and his care, but Manchester United can give him that, they've got a history of doing that. I don't see the rush, I don't see the panic.

"I don't know what's been said or promised behind the scenes, but from the outside this stinks to me that someone is pushing, forcing and rushing it. And I don't think it's going to help the kid in any way, shape or form.

"As a say, I'm a big rival of Manchester United, but I've watched Manchester United from afar, there's top coaches there, top people. I know Michael Carrick very well and, if this kid was ready, he'd be getting played."

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi launches stunning Tottenham rant - 'Most fragile team I've coached'
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi launches stunning Tottenham rant - 'Most fragile team I've coached'

Tottenham look set for another nightmare season, having failed to win in any of their opening five Premier League games of the season, and Roberto De Zerbi is far from happy

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi has endured a miserable second season with Tottenham (Image: Getty Images)

Roberto De Zerbi has sensationally claimed that Tottenham are the ‘most fragile’ team he has ever coached. The Italian has endured a difficult second season in North London, having kept the side up in the Premier League last term.

‌



But Saturday’s 3-2 defeat against Aston Villa has left Spurs without a win in their opening five league games of the campaign and leaves them in the relegation zone.

‌



In assessing his side’s latest reverse, boss De Zerbi made the extraordinarily claim that Spurs were the most mentally fragile side that he has coached throughout his entire career.

‌



"It's a mental aspect for sure, but they have the right mentality," the Italian told talkSPORT. "They work very well, they are good players.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“It's difficult to explain because, in my career, 14 years as a coach, I've never seen one team like us. So fragile, so inconsistent.

"You're good, or you're bad. You can't be very good in the first 30, 40 minutes, and then concede like this in this way. It's tough to accept for me."

Asked where his side went wrong against Aston Villa, he added: "Listen, I'm a coach, but I do not have all the answers...for your question, I have no answer.

‌



"I can say what I think, what I've seen today and I saw my team in the first half play very well, we had chances to score. We didn't score and then we conceded the first goal...we have to stay closer and stay stronger, more compact.

View 2 Images Spurs are now sat in the Premier League relegation zone (Image: Getty Images)

"In the second half, after Kudus' goal, I don't know if the players lost energy...now we have to explain another defeat."

‌



De Zerbi then also suggested that the blame could lay at the players’ doors, with Spurs lacking leaders. He said: "Maybe the communication between the players [is the problem], maybe the leaders have to be stronger.

"We need leaders to drive and lead the team...I don't know, I want to speak with the players when I stay with them. With Newcastle it was the same, in Liverpool it was the same, with Everton it was the same...we have to find the solutions."

Spurs now head into the first international break of the season in the drop zone after their horrendous start. Their first game after the enforced break sees them come up against Manchester United at Old Trafford.
